长风万里，终度玉门。你来到了那座巍峨的城关之下。此刻，它已不是难以越过的雄关天堑，而是春风西行的驿站。在旌旗飘扬的风沙里，你仿佛又一次看到了那位白头将军，正站在城墙之上，远眺东方。他眼里所见，心中所念，口中所说的皆为一句话：长安，如今可好？你踌躇半晌，开口道……
#Y【我没去过长安。】你不忍告诉将军实情，只好说自己还没去过那座举世无双的城。若有机会，你也想漫步在长安城中，去看看世上最绮丽的浮华幻梦。——这是你的真心话。#E
听闻你的回答，将军颔首沉吟，眼中似有热泪。“长安……是个很好，很好的地方。”将军浑厚苍凉的嗓音里带着怀念，也带着慨然。满城少年变白发，手中的锋镞依然，归唐之心依然。城中传来阵阵鼓声，似有千军万马列阵。你听不清他们口中呼喊的名字，但你知道，那是千万乡音汇成的两个字——长安。
en:
The endless winds travel thousands of miles, finally passing through Jade Gate Pass. You arrive beneath that towering fortress. It is no longer an impassable stronghold, but a waystation for the spring breeze journeying west. In the windblown sand, with banners snapping overhead, you seem to glimpse the white-haired general once more, standing atop the wall and gazing east. What he sees in his eyes, holds in his heart, and speaks on his lips all resolve into a single refrain: "How fares Chang'an now?" You hesitate for a long while and say...
#Y[I've never been to Chang'an.] You cannot bear to tell the general the truth, so you simply say you have never been to that peerless city. If given the chance, you too would like to stroll through Chang'an to witness the most dazzling dream of worldly splendor. This is your honest truth.#E
Hearing your answer, the general nods in silent thought, tears seemingly welling in his eyes. "Chang'an... is a very, very fine place." The general's deep and desolate voice carries a sense of nostalgia, as well as a profound sorrow. The youths of the city have turned white-haired, yet the weapons in their hands remain sharp, as does their resolve to return to the Tang. From within the city comes the rolling beat of drums, as if an army of thousands were falling into formation. You cannot clearly hear the name they cry, but you know it is a single name formed by thousands of homesick voices: Chang'an.

en:
Rumors in the palace say the ancient trees in the Rear Garden are haunted. When a long yowl rings out, cats from every corner gather as if attending court. They call it the "Cat Emperor" showing itself. Yet no one claims to have seen its true face.
Some say it is a Tang-era cat demon, one that has watched the throne change hands and stayed indifferent to rise and fall alike. Only the pure of heart can catch a glimpse, if only for an instant. Those lost in power and desire will see nothing but vermilion walls shut tight.
Others scoff. If you have time for ghost stories, you would do better to hustle for a better post.
But those who have truly seen it know this. No matter how the world turns or the years pass, it is always there beneath the tree, waiting for a playmate with a heart as true as its own.

zh:
同光三年，八月二十五日
自六月积雨，七十五日方停，门中心忧黄河，命我出山一探。长老赠白银千两，用以赈灾。何需千两？十两足以。山外自有人“送钱上门”。

同光三年，八月二十六日
路遇灾民，赠饼十张，耗银一两。

同光三年，八月二十七日
路遇灾民，赠饼二十五张，耗银二两五钱。

同光三年，八月二十八日
路遇灾民，赠饼三十张，耗银四两，该死，粮价疯涨。劫匪在何处，我的钱袋子又在何处？

同光三年，八月二十九日
路遇灾民，赠饼十八张，银钱耗尽，未遇劫匪。

同光三年，八月三十日
天地茫茫，饥肠辘辘，不见劫匪。念墨门，念长老，念那九百九十九两白银。

同光三年，八月三十一日
仍不见劫匪。外衣早已典当，无妨，饥火烧肠，不觉冷。

同光三年，九月初一
饿。听闻山中有劫匪聚点，狂喜奔至，却只见遍地饿殍。半晌奔波，只得一破碗，我亦成灾民矣。

同光三年，九月初二
饿。于黄河畔遇一少年，名曰丰能奇。此人水性奇绝，负沙袋于水中亦可穿梭自如，更能徒手捉鱼，羡煞。

同光三年，九月初三
饿极。丰能奇竟识墨门机巧，欲学机关术。墨门机关术岂能随便外传？无礼之徒，心不诚。

同光三年，九月初四
吃鱼三条。丰能奇言学机关术乃为修复堤坝。其虽品性上佳，然墨家机关术不得外传……

同光三年，九月初五
吃鱼五条。此人乃璞玉浑金，无法雕琢着实可惜。我允其同行，每每把玩机巧，任其自学。其中欢喜，不足为外人道。
en:
25th day of the Eighth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
The torrential rains that began in the sixth month have finally stopped after seventy-five days. Worried about the Yellow River, Mohist Hill ordered me out to investigate. The Elder gave me a thousand taels of silver for disaster relief. Why a thousand? Ten would be enough. Beyond the mountain, there are always people eager to "deliver money" to my door.
 
26th day of the Eighth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Encountered refugees. Gave them ten flatbreads; spent one tael.
 
27th day of the Eighth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Encountered refugees. Gave out twenty-five flatbreads; spent two taels and five qian.
 
28th day of the Eighth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Encountered refugees. Gave out thirty flatbreads; spent four taels. Blast it, grain prices are soaring. Where are the bandits, and where is my coin purse?
 
29th day of the Eighth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Encountered refugees. Gave out eighteen flatbreads. My own money is exhausted, and I haven't seen a single bandit.
 
30th day of the Eighth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
The world is vast, and my stomach is empty. Not a bandit in sight. I miss Mohist Hill, I miss the Elder, and I miss those nine hundred and ninety-nine taels of silver.
 
31st day of the Eighth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Still no bandits. I pawned my outer coat a while ago. It matters not; the fire of hunger burns so fiercely I don't feel the cold.
 
1st day of the Ninth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Hungry. Heard there was a bandit camp in the mountains. I rushed there in ecstasy, only to find the ground littered with the starved dead. After running around for half a day, all I got was a cracked bowl. I, too, have become a refugee.
 
2nd day of the Ninth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Hungry. Met a young man by the Yellow River named Feng Nengqi. His swimming skills are phenomenal. He can navigate the currents with ease while carrying sandbags and catch fish barehanded. I am so envious.
 
3rd day of the Ninth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Famished. Feng Nengqi actually recognized my Mohist mechanisms and wants to learn our mechanical arts. How can the secrets of Mohist Hill be taught so casually? What an insolent and insincere fellow.
 
4th day of the Ninth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Ate three fish. Feng Nengqi said he wants to learn mechanisms to repair the river dikes. Though his character is commendable, Mohist arts must never be shared with outsiders...
 
5th day of the Ninth Month, Year 3 of Tongguang
Ate five fish. This man is a piece of uncarved jade; it would be a true pity not to sculpt him. I permitted him to travel with me. I often toy with my gadgets and let him figure them out on his own. The quiet joy in this is something I cannot explain to others.
Ji Xianxing

有那样一把好刀的人，唯有世间的好酒才可相配。若是要去见刀哥，你定要准备一壶……
#Y丰和春。这是江叔提起过的酒，也是陈叔念念不忘的味道。你再无机会与刀哥一起策马江南，但共饮一杯江南酒，可算同行。#E
你提着酒壶来到刀哥坟前，替他去了碑上的落叶。你记得在瓷窑初见时他的嘲讽，也记得在破庙中他的坦诚。你们说好一起要去江湖，去看看外面的世界。可他却像闯入你生活里的一场风暴，轰轰烈烈为你揭开了江湖的一角，然后便消散世间。是的，消散，如日光下的雪，似流水中的盐，无从搜寻。唯有一身怅然，尽付壶中酒。
en:
The Drunken Immortal Month is always bustling with life. The waiter pours Parting Tears for wanderers from all corners of the world, who are trading stories of their travels in varying accents. When they drain their cups, all words soften into contented sighs. You think of Blade's last visit and the cup you never poured for him.
A man with such a fine blade deserves only the finest wine in the world. If you are going to see Blade, you must prepare a pot of...
#YSpring's Bounty. This is the wine Uncle Jiang spoke of, and the flavor Uncle Chen longed for. You will never have the chance to roam on horseback in Jiangnan with Blade again, yet still, one shared cup would be enough.#E
You bring a wine pot to Blade's grave and brush the fallen leaves from his tombstone. You remember his sneer when you first met at the porcelain kiln, and his blunt honesty in the ruined temple. You had agreed to venture into the jianghu together, to see the world outside. Yet he burst into your life like a fierce storm, dramatically tearing back a corner of the jianghu for you, only to vanish from this earth. Yes, he vanished, like snow under sunlight or salt in flowing water, nowhere to be found, leaving you with nothing but a deep sorrow, all poured into the wine in your pot.

zh: 自那以后，那孩子便跟上了他。他也从那孩子身上，逐渐找回了身为人的情感。为了养活彼此，也不想稚子跟着一起动荡，他决定退隐。而以何为生？不如就做鱼脍吧。那一条鱼救了稚子一命，何不也是救了他呢？他的名字早已忘记，但依稀记得姓陈。于是江湖中多了一个快刀鱼脍摊主，大刀陈。
en: From then on, the child followed him everywhere. While looking after the boy, he started to reclaim his own sense of humanity. To give them both a chance at a quieter life and to keep the child away from growing up the way he did, he decided to leave his old path behind. But what now? Why not make a living with the one thing he knew—slicing fish? After all, that fish had saved the boy's life, and maybe, in a way, his own too. He'd long forgotten his given name, but he vaguely remembered his family name was Chen. And so, a new face appeared in town: Broadsword Chen, the sliced fish vendor known for his lightning-fast sword.

听听，多么响亮帅气的名号！看看，多么得百姓拥戴的侠士！心中有明月，手可摘星辰！有她摘星手出手，管他什么张府李府王府的，那些从百姓口袋里夺走的钱财，一分一分她都会摘回来！
那便是魏芷昔作为“摘星手”的二八年华，璀璨耀眼，肆意张扬。

然而狼山一战，大雪封山，铁骑犯境，百姓流离。当赵普逆着满山风雪，一步步行至魏芷昔藏身的山中洞穴时，魏芷昔擦拭着手中染血的长刀，抬头冲他笑了笑……笑过之后却有些想哭。
那便是魏芷昔作为“摘星手”的最后一年，她有些疲惫，有些想家。

世间飞鸟，本该将一生用于遨游。
然当飞鸟心中有了困惑和迟疑，当飞鸟意识到仅凭自己一双翅膀，无法护佑住天下万民之时，世间便再无此飞鸟。
但世间也从此多了一位坐于后堂间，与夫婿共同寻求救民之法的夫人。
en:
When the pageboy rushed in with news that the "Star Stealer" moniker was stirring up a storm across the jianghu, Wei Zhixi was drinking atop a high tower. She wiped down her throwing star, struggling to suppress a grin.
Listen to that! What a resounding, dashing alias! Look at how the common folk adore this hero! In heart the moon shines bright, with hands the stars take flight. With the Star Stealer around, no matter which noble household, Zhang, Li, or Wang, she'd reclaim every copper coin stolen from the people, piece by piece!
Such were Wei Zhixi's "Star Stealer" years, radiant, untamed, and dazzling.

Yet the Battle of Wolf Mountain changed everything. Blizzards sealed the peaks, iron cavalry trampled the land, and refugees scattered like leaves. When Zhao Pu trudged through the snow-laden winds to the mountain cave where Wei Zhixi hid, she looked up from wiping her bloodstained blade and flashed him a smile... and then felt like crying.
That was the last year of Wei Zhixi as the "Star Stealer". She was tired. She longed for home.

A bird born to soar should spend its life in flight.
But when the bird doubts, when it realizes its wings alone cannot shield all under heaven, such a bird ceases to exist. 
Yet the world gained a new lady: one who sits in the inner hall with her husband, together seeking ways to save the people.

en:
During the event, spend Echo Beads to buy [Lotus Pouches]. Open a [Lotus Pouch] to receive either 1 [Lucky Turtle] or another reward.
If you get a [Lucky Turtle] and trigger a Match, Three-in-a-Row, or All Clear, you will receive [Lotus Cheer] and some [Lotus Pouches] back. Refunded [Lotus Pouches] are opened immediately and will not be added to your inventory.
[Lotus Cheer] can be exchanged in the event shop for limited cosmetics and other rewards. Each character can buy up to 1,400 [Lotus Pouches], not including those obtained through refunds. The 3x3 board starts with 8 different [Lucky Turtles].
If a [Lotus Pouch] gives an item reward, you will not receive a [Lucky Turtle].
After the event ends, purchased [Lotus Pouches] will be automatically reclaimed at a rate of 16 for 1 [Lingering Melody: Bind]. Any remaining [Lotus Pouches] fewer than 16 will be converted into Echo Jade at a rate of 1:10.
After the event ends, you can still exchange rewards until the shop closes, but you can no longer Pray. Any unused [Lotus Cheer] will be automatically converted into Echo Jade at a rate of 16:1.
Pray 2 times to receive the gift accessory [Lucky Turtle Charm]. Spend [Glaze Palette] in [Pottery Styling] to unlock more [Lucky Turtle Charm] styles.

zh:
妙乌喜欢自己的名字，也喜欢给它名字的僧人。
那僧人说，生活在这璧泉山上的猫咪，都很有灵性。
那僧人还说，妙乌是他见过的，最聪明、最有灵性、最妙的一只。
妙乌很骄傲。它日夜穿山林，见天地，追日月，听佛音……当然是一只妙喵喵！
但作为一只妙喵喵，它有一事参不透。不知为何，那僧人许久没来找它了。
妙乌不知道那僧人去了哪，只好在原地等他，一年又一年的……哼，它才不是想念那人呢，它只是无事可做，顺便等等。
再说了，她有自己的笨蛋妹妹陪着，这山林还有好多有趣小猫咪，日子一点都不枯燥！这不，那台上的三只，又开始它们的表演啦！
en:
Marvel Meow is fond of its name, and of the monk who gave it.
The monk once said that all the cats living on Jadebrook Mountain had a touch of the divine.
He also said Marvel Meow was the cleverest, most gifted, most marvelous one he'd ever met.
Marvel Meow is proud. It roams through the woods day and night, chasing the sun and moon, listening to the worldly sound... All these make it a marvelous Meow Meow!
But even a marvelous Meow Meow has things it can't figure out. Why hasn't the monk shown up for so long?
It doesn't know where he's gone, so it stays put and waits, year after year... Hmph! It isn't that it misses him. It just has nothing better to do, that's all.
Besides, it has its silly little sister for company, and there are always plenty of interesting cats in the forest. Life is far from boring! Look, those three on the stage are starting their show again!

zh:
游侠，见字如面。
前些时日，老朽随府尹大人巡查蒙学，见学堂里的娃娃们一个个正襟危坐，埋首书卷，连我等走近了都未曾察觉。
老朽心下好奇，是何等妙文，能让这些上蹿下跳的娃娃们如此专心？一问才知，他们手中所读，竟是你前些时日所赠。
老朽又问，这些书好在何处？娃娃们七嘴八舌，老朽这才知道，原来你竟为每个孩子都择了不同的书，实在是费心了。而听闻老朽与你相熟，他们都央着我，定要代他们向你道声谢。
只是，真要问他们想说什么，这群小家伙却面露羞赧，讷讷而止了。最后，老朽想了个法子，让他们把想说的话都诉诸笔端，一并封在信里了。至于写了什么，老朽绝未偷看！
对了，娃娃们还托我转交几幅画作，说是读了书卷后的有感而发。他们都说，游侠你是他们见过最有眼光的人，定能欣赏他们的大作。
哈哈，看来往后若再有与孩子们打交道的差事，找游侠准是没错了。
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/68ce3f34f8a6f9cbb28dc427y9jXfbBw06' size='2000*1452' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
<IMAGE id='im2' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/68ce3f3d586876553bf1a834KzPaop0306' size='1401*1872' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Dear Wanderer,

The other day, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the village school. The children sat straight at their desks, noses buried in scrolls, so absorbed they didn't even notice us draw near.
Curious what could hold their attention so completely, I asked. Turns out, they were reading the very books you gifted them not long ago.
I inquired further: what made these books so special? The little ones burst into chatter, and that's when I learned you had chosen a different book for each child. What thoughtfulness.
When they heard I knew you, they begged me to pass along their thanks.
But when I asked what they wanted to say, shyness took over, and words failed them. So I suggested they write it down instead. Their letters are enclosed. And no, I did not peek!
Oh, and they also asked me to send you a few drawings. Inspired, they said, by your books. They all agreed you're the most discerning person they've ever met, and that you'd surely appreciate their masterpieces.
Seems to me, whenever there's a task involving children, you're the one to call.

将仲子

叔于田

叔于狩，巷无饮酒。岂无饮酒？不如叔也，洵美且好。

大叔于田

大叔于田，乘乘马，执辔如组，两骖如舞。叔在薮，火烈具举。禅裼暴虎，献于公所。将叔无狃，戒其伤女。

en:
【Airs of the States - Airs of Zheng】

Black Robes

How fine the black robes look! When they are worn out, I will make new ones for you. I will go to your official residence; upon my return, I will present you with a feast.
How good the black robes are! When they are worn out, I will remake them for you. I will go to your official residence; upon my return, I will present you with a feast.
How grand the black robes appear! When they are worn out, I will rework them for you. I will go to your official residence; upon my return, I will present you with a feast.

I Beg of You, Zhongzi

I beg of you, Zhongzi, do not climb into our village, do not break our willow trees. It's not that I dare to cherish them, but I fear my parents. You, Zhongzi, are dear to me, but the words of my parents are also to be feared.

Shu Goes to the Fields

Shu has gone to the fields, and the lanes seem empty of dwellers. Are there truly no dwellers? None compare to Shu, so handsome and kind.
Shu has gone hunting, and the lanes seem empty of drinkers. Are there truly no drinkers? None compare to Shu, so handsome and fine.
Shu has gone to the wilds, and the lanes seem empty of horsemen. Are there truly no horsemen? None compare to Shu, so handsome and brave.

Elder Shu Goes to the Fields

Elder Shu goes to the fields, driving a team of four horses, holding the reins as if weaving, the two outer horses dancing. Shu is in the marsh, fires blazing all around. Baring his arms, he subdues a tiger, presenting it at the lord's place. I urge Shu not to be reckless, lest it injure you.
Shu goes to the fields, driving a team of yellow horses. The two inner horses lead proudly, the two outer horses fly in formation. Shu is in the marsh, fires blazing high. Shu is skilled at shooting, and also excellent at driving, now reining in, now letting go.
Shu goes to the fields, driving a team of dappled horses. The two inner horses keep pace, the two outer horses move like hands. Shu is in the marsh, fires blazing fiercely. Shu's horses slow down, Shu's arrows grow rare, now he loosens the quiver, now he puts away the bow.

So I became a mirror—and only when the mirror shattered did I realize the moon's light was brighter than I ever knew. 
Now I have become the moon, rising through skies, bathed in clear, gentle radiance—unshaken by roaring snows or howling winds. 
I don't chase the rushing river of time. Wherever the moon graces a thousand streams, there I am—shining together with all living things.

今日天晴风朗，老履翁颠了颠筐里的靴履，晃晃悠悠去了市集。
“老翁，你这鞋里是镶了金？怎卖这么贵？”
同样的话，老履翁在过去三十来年已经听太多了。但他也不在意，只是闭着眼睛摇头晃脑，感受春光照面的舒适。

“这鞋怎么卖。”又是一个问价的女声。
老履翁眼也没睁，只当和之前看热闹图新奇的人一样，张口就来：“一百。”
“我买了。”
“嗯嗯，买不起就走吧，这鞋就这价......你买了？！”老履翁反应过来，猛地睁开眼，只见眼前站了个面色冷冷的姑娘，正在认真瞧着手上的鞋。

老履翁走南闯北这么些年，只消一眼他就确定，这姑娘是真心喜爱他做的鞋。老履翁顿时笑开了，这么些年，终于又遇到一个懂鞋的人了。
“你这鞋摸起来舒服，鞋底也软厚。这是怎么做的？”
老翁眼睛又亮。问制鞋之道？知己呀！

“咳咳，看姑娘你也懂些做鞋的门道，那想必你也清楚，制鞋绝非易事。你看，若是皮革为面，则需数月鞣制；若是亚麻为皮，则需经沤麻、绩麻等工序；遑论纳千层之底，则需针、锥、木楦等工具，用蜡线穿透多层布，费劲得很。你手上那双，就是标标准准的千层底啦，对于远行者而言，是最好的选择。这双鞋，老头子我做了整一年呐！”
一年，那是很久了。女子摸了摸手上的鞋，低着头，眼睛却落在旁处。

“如果想正合脚，那就要将鞋帮与木底弯曲定型，误差需控制在毫厘之间。这样做出来的才是真正合适的鞋。做鞋子啊，还是得心细。姑娘，你说是不？”
是，得心细些，女子想。
但倘若是位走南闯北的父亲，独自一人拉扯病弱的孩子寻药，那这其中苦楚，又岂是一句心细就能说清道明的。

“不过说到底，做鞋子，最重要的，就是心呐...”老履翁望着对街正给女儿喂水的父亲，像是想起了什么人，声音悠远。
“一百。”兰澳将钱递给老履翁，“谢谢。”
“哎！你这小姑娘还真给呀？快拿回去，不用这么多！”老履翁赶忙出声。
女人没回应他，转身准备离开。
见她也没收回去的意思，老履翁又说：“要不你再拿两双走？这俩也不错呀！姑娘？姑娘？”
“不必。”兰澳的背影顿了顿,“我也会。”

老履翁双手拿着两双鞋，半晌没能再开口。
女人越走越远了。
恍惚间，他好似又看见了当年那个问他怎么做鞋的男人。
en:
On a bright, breezy day, the old shoemaker gently shifted the basket of boots balanced on his back and strolled slowly to the bustling marketplace. 
"Old man, are these shoes lined with gold? Why are they so pricey?" 
For over thirty years, he'd heard that question more times than he cared to count. But he didn't mind. Closing his eyes, he swayed lightly, basking in the warm spring sunshine. 

"How much for these shoes?" another woman's voice called out. 
"One hundred," he answered absently, without opening his eyes, assuming it was just another curious onlooker. 
"I'll take them." 
"If you can't afford them, just move along. That's the price... Wait, you're buying them?!" Startled, the old man opened his eyes and saw a young woman standing before him, her face serious as she carefully examined the shoes in her hands. 

Having traveled far and wide, the old shoemaker knew at once this woman truly appreciated the craftsmanship behind his work. A smile, warm and genuine, spread across his face—it had been years since someone truly understood the art of shoemaking. 
"These shoes feel so soft and comfortable, and the soles are thick but supple. How do you make them?" 
His eyes brightened. A fellow craftsperson? A kindred spirit! 

"Ah, my dear, since you know a thing or two about shoemaking, you understand it's no simple task. If leather is used for the uppers, it takes months to tan it properly. If linen, there are soaking and weaving steps to consider. And the thousand-layer soles? They require needles, awls, wooden lasts, and waxed thread to stitch through countless layers of fabric. It's painstaking work. This pair you hold is the quintessential thousand-layer sole—perfect for travelers. I spent a whole year making these." 
A whole year—that's a long time. The woman ran her fingers lightly over the shoes, lowering her gaze but her eyes drifting elsewhere. 

"To fit just right, the shoe's upper must be shaped and bent to the wooden sole with precision—off by even a fraction of a millimeter, and the fit's ruined. Shoemaking demands patience and care, don't you think?" 
Yes, she thought quietly—attention to detail is everything. 
Yet, what if this shoe was for a father journeying endlessly, alone, caring for a sick child in search of medicine? Such hardship couldn't simply be measured by careful work alone. 

"But in the end," the shoemaker said softly, gazing across the street at a father giving water to his daughter, "what matters most in shoemaking is heart..." 
"One hundred," Lan Ao said, placing the money in his hand. "Thank you." 
"Oh! You're too kind, young lady! Here, take it back—you don't need to pay so much!" the old man urged. 
She didn't reply, turning to walk away. 
Seeing she wasn't going to take it back, he called out, "How about two more pairs? These are good ones as well! Miss? Miss?" 
"No, thank you," Lan Ao paused, then added, "I make shoes myself." 

The old shoemaker stood holding two pairs in his hands, words failing him. 
She walked farther and farther away. 
For a moment, he thought he saw, in the distance, the man who long ago asked him how he made shoes—a memory stirred, as timeless as his craft.
Ode to Great Harvest
Assassin's Memory: Deep in Their Cups

滞留唐国那三年，他伪装成重刑囚犯，在狱中采石苦劳。
同样被困于牢狱的老人看着他，眼中有一丝嘲弄的笑意。“难道你这辈子，就没有过在意的人？与那人在一起，便会希望时间慢一些、长一些。”
他手中采石的锹子顿了一顿，突然想起那个蒙住双眼的女子，很短，只有一瞬。
“没有，大事未做，还想不到这些。”

“好了，时候到了，你终于可回去了。等很久了吧，一直想着你的大事。”
嗯。他短短应一声，来不及道别，转身上马。
他要回去，蹉跎滞留了三年，计划不可再拖。
但是在那之前，还有另一件事。
他利落地收刀、甩血，将手中湿热的眼睛擦干净，小心地放进那个极寒极冷的寒玉匣，揣入怀里。
他想起三年前定下约定的那一天，他初见她，在湖底。
他向她说着所求之事，她静静听着。明明双眼看不见，却直直望向他的方向，似乎可以一下看到他内心最深处。
有一下重重的心跳。
他有一瞬间失神，听不见她的回应。不过所幸，她的回答很好懂，无论他说什么，她都答好。
久闻月神大名，不知可否帮我救一人？
好。
救这个人，可能要杀很多其他人，都是好人。
好。
月神果然如传闻所言……不知月神想要什么回报？一对眼睛？
好。
于是定下约定，她帮他护人，他帮她寻眼。
只可惜晚了三年，希望她不要怪。
他终于到了月湖，对着依旧清澈的湖水，突然抬手理了一下自己的头发。
风尘仆仆的，太糙。

他还是晚了一步，又或者，是很多步。
整整三年。
三年前，他等了她三天，而她却在湖底，等他到如今。
还不清，如何还得清？
但他答应过的，一定会做到，哪怕、哪怕……
他写信的手微微颤抖。
我会给你换眼。
他写下最后的落款，黎蓁蓁，嘴唇轻碰，无声念出来。
我会给你换眼。
他离开了湖底，却还最后转身望了一眼。
可惜，没能见到她复明的样子，没能见到她眼中，映出自己的身影。
可惜，若是当初……可惜，没有若是。
en:
For three years, he'd played the role of a hardened prisoner, breaking stones in the prison quarry.
The old man sharing his captivity watched him with amused eyes. "Never had someone who mattered to you? Someone who made you wish time would slow down?"
His shovel hesitated mid-strike. A fleeting image surfaced—a woman with blindfolded eyes. Just for an instant.
"No," he answered. "Not with unfinished business at hand."

"Time's up then," the old man said. "You're free to go. Must be eager to attend to your grand affairs."
A grunt of acknowledgment. No time for goodbyes. He mounted his horse without looking back.
Three wasted years. His plans couldn't wait any longer.
But first, one last task.
With practiced motions, he cleaned his blade, wiped the still-warm eyes, and placed them carefully in the ice-cold jade box against his chest.
He remembered their first meeting at the lake's bottom three years prior.
As he explained his request, she listened quietly. Though blindfolded, her gaze seemed to pierce straight through him.
A single, jarring heartbeat.
For a moment, he'd forgotten to listen for her reply. Not that it mattered. Her answer was always the same.
Long have I heard of the Moon Goddess. Will you help me save someone?
Yes.
To save this person... I may have to kill many others. Good people.
Yes.
The Moon Goddess is indeed as rumored... What repayment would you ask? A pair of eyes?
Yes.
Their bargain was struck: she'd guard his charge; he'd procure her new eyes.
A pity he was three years late. He hoped she wouldn't resent it.
When he finally reached Moon Lake, its waters remained impossibly clear. He suddenly smoothed his wind-tangled hair.
Too rough. Too wind-worn.

He was late. Or perhaps late was an understatement.
Three years.
Three years ago, he waited three days for her. But she, at the bottom of the lake, had waited for him until now.
How could such a debt ever be repaid?
Yet he had promised. He would see it through. Even if, even if...His hand trembled slightly as he wrote:
I will give you new eyes.
He signed it Li Zhenzhen, lips forming the name soundlessly.
I will give you new eyes.
Departing the depths, he cast one final glance backward.
A pity, never seeing her restored sight. A pity, never seeing his reflection in her eyes.
A pity that if only...But no. If only changed nothing.
Song of Treasure Basin

zh:
人与人的相遇分很多种，其中一种，像草叶上的露珠。 
太阳落山时，细小的水滴在草叶上凝结，滚动到一起，这便是相遇了。 
夜里的客栈是欢乐的，歌声，舞女，流水般轮转的酒水和菜肴慰藉着行客们的胃和寂寞。沉默的龟兹游商没有说话，他只是坐在角落里，垂着头盯着自己那双格外大的脚看。 
“咳咳……客人要跳舞吗……只要一贯钱……我是跳的最好的……” 
这是她对他说的第一句话。 
这是个露珠一样的女人。脆弱，晶莹，弯下腰颤抖着咳嗽，似乎马上就要被日光蒸发。但她眼里燃着两簇倔强的鬼火，她拼了命的活下去，活下去就有希望回到家乡。而他却是截然相反的人：高大却温吞，对人生中的一切逆来顺受——除了不愿意再回到家。他想，或许老天爷弄错了。或许他才是会随着太阳升起而无声无息蒸发的露珠。 
但其实老天很会开玩笑。她没被严酷风沙，千里跋涉和阴魂不散的病魔打败。她死在天宝十五年六月的战火里。 
所以，还是她死的早些。 
白姓的龟兹游商——现在他是一名乐手了——带着她的遗物走了回去，回他原本一辈子都不想回的地方。只是她的家太遥远了，他寻觅了很久都没找到她口中那个在春天会跳舞的部落。而他也终于开始感到太阳在地平线下蠢蠢欲动的脉搏了。 
在太阳升起之前，他带着她的遗物回到了那间客栈。第二天早上，第一缕阳光照在草叶上的时候，两滴干枯的露珠并在一起蒸发了。 
薤上露，何易晞！露晞明朝更复落，人死一去何时归？
en:
There are many kinds of encounters between people. One kind is like dewdrops on a blade of grass.  
When the sun sets, tiny droplets condense on the grass blades and roll together, this is their meeting.  
The inn at night was merry. Songs, dancing girls, wine and dishes flowing like water consoled the travelers' stomachs and loneliness. The silent Kucha itinerant trader did not speak. He merely sat in the corner, head bowed, staring at his unusually large feet.  
"Cough cough... Would you like to dance, guest... Only one string of coins... I dance the best..."  
This was the first sentence she spoke to him.  
She was a woman like a dewdrop. Fragile, translucent, bending over with trembling coughs as if about to evaporate under sunlight. But two stubborn ghost fires burned in her eyes, she struggled desperately to live, for survival held the hope of returning home. He, however, was the complete opposite, tall yet placid, accepting everything in life with passive resignation, except for refusing to return home. He thought perhaps Heaven had made a mistake. Perhaps he was the dewdrop that would vanish silently with the rising sun.  
But in truth, Heaven plays cruel jokes. She was not defeated by harsh sandstorms, thousand-mile treks, or lingering illness. She died in the war in the sixth month of the 15th year of Tianbao.  
So, in the end, she died earlier.  
The Kucha trader surnamed Bai, now a musician, carried her belongings back, returning to the place he originally never wanted to revisit in his lifetime. Only, her home was too distant; he searched for a long time but never found the tribe she spoke of, the one that would dance in spring. And he finally began to feel the sun's restless pulse stirring beneath the horizon.  
Before the sun rose, he brought her belongings back to that inn. The next morning, when the first rays of sunlight touched the blades of grass, two dried dewdrops merged and evaporated together.  
Dew on the garlic leaves, how easily you dry! Dew dries today but falls again tomorrow at dawn, but once a person dies, when will they ever return?

zh:
孟宽习惯性地抄起腰间酒葫芦晃了晃，空的。
“哎……”他长叹一声，“好汉没了酒，就好比火烧没了肉，憋屈！”
秀姑娘闻言自图纸里抬首，莞尔道：“谁说好汉就得喝酒？你看启昭，就从来不沾酒。启昭，你的规尺——”
“谁说启昭不喝酒，他那水囊之中，说不准盛的便是——”
话音未落，一个水囊砸进他怀里，不偏不倚，如同尺量过。
“哎哟，还是启昭兄弟疼我！”孟宽面有得色，晃了晃水囊，拔开塞子正欲痛饮，“此盖一开，我便知晓，里头装的准是你们那的千日醉，今日总算有口——”
一语未毕，他眉头忽皱，砸摸两下嘴道：“娘的，怎地这般寡淡？你拿好酒兑水了？糟蹋，太糟蹋了。”
孟宽拍了拍身旁瘦骨嶙峋的老马，将水囊凑至它嘴边：“兄弟，这淡得够给你了！”
马打了个响鼻，不理他。
恰在此时，傅千里从不远处而来。孟宽眼睛一亮，把水囊朝她丢了过去，嘿嘿一笑：“接着！好东西，省着点喝！”
傅千里抬手接住，随意一掂，便知内里已去大半。她面色如常，只淡淡瞥了孟宽一眼，拔开盖子喝了两口。手臂一扬，将水囊掷与秀姑娘。
“谁说好酒只能配好汉，我辈女儿家，亦饮得。”
孟宽一拍大腿，朗声大笑，火光将众人的影子拉得又斜又长…… 

若是尘烟已定山河无恙，他们或真能策马同游，去大江南北、去喝遍各地的好酒。
en:
Meng Kuan shook the wine gourd at his waist out of habit. Empty.
"Sigh," he groaned. "A hero without wine is like a meat bun with no meat. Utterly miserable!"
Hearing this, Miss Xiu looked up from her blueprints and smiled. "Who says heroes must drink? Look at Qi Zhao; he never touches a drop. Qi Zhao, where is your ruler?"
"Who says Qi Zhao doesn't drink? That waterskin of his might well contain..."
Before he could finish, a waterskin flew into his arms, landing with perfect precision.
"Haha! Brother Qi Zhao truly knows me!" Meng Kuan smirked, shaking the waterskin. He pulled the stopper, ready to take a deep gulp. "Once this is open, I know it's the Sweet Slumber from your hometown. Finally, a taste of..."
He stopped mid-gulp, furrowing his brow and smacking his lips. "Damn, why is it so watery? Did you dilute good wine? What a waste!"
Meng Kuan patted his scrawny old horse and held the skin to its mouth. "Here, friend, this is thin enough even for you!"
The horse snorted and ignored him.
Just then, Fu Qianli approached. Meng Kuan's eyes lit up and he tossed the skin to her. "Catch! Good stuff, drink sparingly!"
Fu Qianli caught it and knew it was mostly empty. Her expression unchanged, she gave Meng Kuan a flat look, pulled the stopper, and took two gulps before tossing it to Miss Xiu.
"Who says fine wine is only for men? We daughters of the Jianghu can drink just as well."
Meng Kuan slapped his thigh and laughed heartily as the firelight stretched their shadows long and thin.

If the dust of war ever settles and the land finds peace, perhaps they will ride together, traveling the world to drink the finest wines of every land.

zh:
觉障林玩法中有特殊的战斗规则，玩家自身的养成属性、道具都不会在局内生效。
玩家需要在局内拾取武器、心法、奇术、药品等来在局内强化自身。各类道具有白、蓝、紫、金四种品质，品质越高效果越强。
随着玩法的进程，玩家可活动的区域将会越来越小，区域外瘴气将会蔓延，进入瘴气的玩家会持续损失生命。玩家需要获取更高品质的道具，利用它们技能之间的配合，并在不同时机选择合理的跑图规划来战胜其它玩家。
与此同时，结算时背包内物品将根据品质及数量转化为罪叶，可在商店里兑换珍稀奖励。
en:
Perception Forest has special combat rules: Players' own development attributes and items will not take effect inside the match. 
You need to pick up weapons, Inner Ways, Mystic Skills, medicines, and other items inside the match to strengthen yourselves. There are four qualities of various items: white, blue, purple, and gold. The higher the quality, the stronger the effect. 
As the match progresses, the area where players can move will shrink, and the miasma outside the area will spread. Players who enter the miasma will continuously lose HP. To defeat other players, you'll need to equip high quality gear, coordinate your skills, and choose reasonable movement paths based on the style of battle. 
At the same time, the items in the bag will be converted into Sin Leaves according to their quality and quantity at the end of the match, which can be exchanged for rare rewards in the shop.

zh:
燕荧自幼敏慧，好读书，十四岁便考中了秀才，乡里人都说燕家出了个文曲星。彼时少年意气、挥斥方遒，正是大展宏图的时候，不料契丹猝然南侵，顷刻间国破家亡。面对残破的家园和苦苦挣扎的乡亲，燕荧恍悟，一味学文救不了这残酷的世道，唯有兵戈方能止战，护下一方安宁。他就此弃文学武，投笔从戎，入了世宗麾下。
军中寂寞，将士们闲时多下象棋排遣一二。燕荧偶得一份残谱，上面用象棋模拟了唐明宗李嗣源击败梁将葛从周的惊世一战。他看后大受启发，将曾经参加过的战局融入棋盘，逐步推演出一套以棋拟战的象征之术。此后燕荧用棋局预演战机，竟屡屡言中。众人啧啧称奇，将他推为北伐军中的智囊，格外尊敬。
en:
Yan Ying is a bright child who loves to read. By the age of fourteen, he had already passed the exam and become a Xiucai (a preliminary scholar). The people in his village often praise Yan's family having a star of Literature. At that time, he was full of youthful ambition, and was about to make a name for himself. But suddenly, the Khitan invaded the south. His country was vanquished in a heartbeat and his family was torn apart. Seeing his homeland in ruins and the villagers struggling to survive, Yan Ying came to realize that mere scholarship could do little to save a broken world. Realizing that only by taking up weapons could he quell the chaos and restore peace, he laid down his brush and took up the sword, joining the army under Emperor Shizong of the Later Zhou Dynasty (the Emperor of Generation).
Life in the army crawled by, and Chinese chess became a small refuge for the soldiers. One day, Yan Ying chanced upon a battered fragment of a Chinese chess manual, where he discovered the story of Emperor Mingzong of the Later Tang Dynasty (Li Siyuan, the Emperor of Wisdom), who had once outwitted General Ge by adapting a strategy from the game to win a legendary battle. Inspired by his battles, he began weaving real encounters into his chess play, crafting a style that mirrored warfare in every move. Before long, Yan Ying's gift for foreseeing battles through the board earned him widespread acclaim as a master strategist throughout the army.

zh:
冯夷原没有生辰，一辈子懒散惯了，便连生辰也忘了个干净，索性便拿朱鱼的生辰，做了自己的。毕竟，阿郑、如之、阿错……不论谁过生辰，下厨的都是冯夷。要擀了细细长长的长寿面，捏了白白胖胖的寿桃，拣着时令菜蔬攒出六菜一汤。不知何时起，冯夷颠勺的日子，已比持刀的日子还多了，以至于刚入龙蛟帮的几位弟兄，直将这“冯老大”当做是伙夫老大，闹了个笑话。

有的事，能不麻烦就不麻烦，可有的事，能麻烦便尽量麻烦。不过对冯夷来说，所谓“有的事”，都是朱鱼的事。没办法，谁叫卖鱼郎赖上了红袖仙呢。要说这“赖”，最讲求对症下药，若学那话本里的肉麻手段，怕不过三回便被扫地出了门。还是九流门的兄弟教得好，“烈女怕缠郎”：她要吃饭，他便是伙夫，寻了江南新出的莼菜与笋同煨，好叫她吃出南方的乡愁来；她要出游，他便是马夫，“借”了万事休的白驹，专过山中琼华盛开处，好叫她一边赏景，一边又寻了入药的杏花来；至于她带的三个娃娃……刚从伙房出来的冯夷擦了擦手，瞧见又多出的孩子，赔了个笑，便又转身回去，重生了炉灶，使断浪刀法切了咸鱼，吊了冬瓜汤的鲜味儿，再细细撒上东海客商刚进的虾皮，待香味扑鼻时，冯夷的笑一定比外头肚子发饿的叫声更响：“好菜来喽——”看着又不知从哪儿来的孩子，冯夷递过了手中的陶碗，罢了罢了，毕竟有人，才有家。

从前冯夷总想：人不是为了别人活，天地逍遥，来去孑然。人，总是为了自己。从前冯夷也不懂她，不懂她为何天天自找麻烦。冯夷问，明明自是凡人一个，为何要贴金涂泥，去做泥塑的菩萨。朱鱼笑笑，回：“泥菩萨，便算不得菩萨么？过河的泥菩萨，非是融在了水里，只是回到了众生。”冯夷咂摸了嘴，有些品不出个中滋味儿。不知不觉，好像冯夷的生活中，早已多出了很多，多出了她、多出了三个孩子、多出了龙蛟帮的上上下下……或许，往后还会多出更多。罢了，若她要做菩萨，他做菩萨身下的青狮白象便是了。若泥菩萨要过河才能救世，这莽莽浑水，便由他来蹚吧。
en:
Feng Yi never had a birthday. He'd lived a lazy life and never bothered to remember one. So in the end, he simply took Zhu Yu's birthday as his own. After all, whether it was A'zheng, Ruzhi, or A'cuo, whenever a birthday rolled around, it was always Feng Yi who ended up in the kitchen. Rolling out fine, slender Longevity Noodles, shaping plump little peach buns, gathering fresh seasonal greens for six dishes and one soup. Somewhere along the way, Feng Yi spent more time at the stove than wielding a sword. To the point when new recruits first joined the Dragon Hall, they even mistook "Boss Feng" for the head chef, causing quite the uproar.

Some things, he thought, are best not to trouble yourself over. And some other things, trouble yourself all you can. But when it came to Zhu Yu, trouble was always something to seek out for Feng Yi. What could he do? The fishmonger had latched onto the Red-Sleeved Fairy. Of course, to latch with persistence, the right tactics are much needed. If he'd tried the sappy nonsense from storybooks, he'd have been tossed out in three days flat. Thankfully, the brothers from Nine Mortal Ways taught him better: A fierce lady fears no brute, but can't resist a man who never leaves. If she needed to eat, he became the cook, simmering fresh watershield and bamboo shoots just to stir her homesick cravings for the South. If she wanted to travel, he became the groom, "borrowing" a white steed from Wan Shixiu, riding only to places where the Qionghua trees bloomed thick in the mountains, so she could admire the blossoms and gather medicinal apricot flowers along the way. As for the three little kids she brought... Fresh from the kitchen, Feng Yi wiped his hands, spotted yet another stray child, and, chuckling awkwardly, turned back to fire up the stove again. Using his Severing Wave technique, he sliced salted fish and brewed a winter melon soup rich with dried shrimp from distant eastern merchants. When the aroma filled the air, his booming voice would always drown out the rumbling stomachs outside:

"Hot food's ready!"

Handing over a clay bowl to yet another child, Feng Yi thought, "Ah, well. Where there are people, there is a home."

Once, Feng Yi believed that a man should live only for himself, free as the wind, coming and going without ties. Once, he couldn't understand her. Couldn't understand why Zhu Yu insisted on taking the burdens of the world onto her shoulders. He asked her, why smear herself with mud and gold to play the bodhisattva as an ordinary person? She smiled and said:

"A clay bodhisattva is still a bodhisattva, is it not? A clay bodhisattva doesn't melt away when crossing the river, it simply returns to the people."

Feng Yi pursed his lips, unable to fully understand the meaning. But without realizing it, his life had filled up, with her, with three children, with the bustling souls of the Dragon Hall. Maybe, in time, there would be even more. Ah, whatever. If she wanted to be a bodhisattva, then he would be the blue lion or white elephant that carried her. If the clay bodhisattva had to cross the river to save the world, then let him be the one to wade through the mud and mire.

zh:
【上经·䷂】

䷂
屯：元亨，利贞；勿用有攸往，利建侯。
《彖》曰：屯，刚柔始交而难生；动乎险中，大亨贞。雷雨之动满盈，天造草昧；宜建侯而不宁。
《象》曰：云雷，屯；君子以经纶。
初九，磐桓，利居贞，利建侯。
《象》曰：虽磐桓，志行正也；以贵下贱，大得民也。
六二，屯如邅如。乘马班如，匪寇婚媾；女子贞不字，十年乃字。
《象》曰：六二之难，乘刚也。“十年乃字”，反常也。
六三，即鹿无虞，惟入于林中，君子几不如舍，往吝。
《象》曰：“即鹿无虞”，以从禽也。君子舍之，往吝穷也。
六四，乘马班如，求婚媾。往吉，无不利。
《象》曰：求而往，明也。
九五，屯其膏，小，贞吉；大，贞凶。
《象》曰：“屯其膏”，施未光也。
上六，乘马班如，泣血涟如。
《象》曰：“泣血涟如”，何可长也。
……
en:
【Upper Canon · Hexagram 3】

Zhun (Difficulty at the Beginning)
Zhun: Supreme success, favorable to be steadfast. Do not use this for seeking advancement; it is favorable to appoint feudal lords.
The Commentary on the Judgment says: Zhun means that hardness and softness begin to interact, and difficulty arises. Movement within peril leads to great success and steadfastness. The movement of thunder and rain fills everything; heaven creates in a state of chaos and obscurity. It is fitting to appoint feudal lords, but there is no peace.
The Commentary on the Image says: Clouds and thunder form Zhun; the superior man thus orders and regulates affairs.
Initial Nine: Hesitating and halting. It is favorable to remain steadfast, and favorable to appoint feudal lords.
The Commentary on the Image says: Though hesitating and halting, the will is set on what is correct. By honoring the lowly, one greatly wins the people.
Six in the Second: Difficulties and entanglements. The horse team turns back. Not a brigand, but a suitor. The woman is steadfast and does not marry; after ten years, she marries.
The Commentary on the Image says: The difficulty of Six in the Second arises from riding on hardness. "After ten years, she marries" — this is a return to the normal course.
Six in the Third: Chasing the deer without a forester, one only enters the forest. The superior man, seeing the opportunity, would rather give up; to go forward brings regret.
The Commentary on the Image says: "Chasing the deer without a forester" means following the game. The superior man gives it up; going forward leads to regret and exhaustion.
Six in the Fourth: The horse team turns back. Seeking a marriage alliance. Going forward brings good fortune; there is nothing unfavorable.
The Commentary on the Image says: Seeking and then going forward is wise.
Nine in the Fifth: Hoarding one's riches. For the small, steadfastness brings good fortune; for the great, steadfastness brings misfortune.
The Commentary on the Image says: "Hoarding one's riches" — the distribution has not yet been made manifest.
Top Six: The horse team turns back. Weeping blood flows in streams.
The Commentary on the Image says: "Weeping blood flows in streams" — how can this last long?
……
Ding Huozi

zh:
韩微在心里描摹了一次又一次那个人。
染血的黄袍，洞开的城门。那人策马而来，马蹄印下一个个弧形的血月，一个接一个，踩着恩义情仇，踩到金銮殿上。而后，这些血色的月牙就像一张笑颜，接着就要咧开大嘴，吞吃了世道，吃了壮年男子的头颅，吃了妇孺手里的炊饼。每一次都这般。
他想来想去，也想不出那张脸不溅满血的样子。是，血。他爹的血，娘的血，韩家满门的血。
想着想着，血竟从妄境中那张脸的眼角流下来了，长长一条，蜿蜒流淌。那个人哭了？怎么会哭呢。他已做了皇帝了，千秋青史将有他一笔了，哭什么？

痛觉传来。噢，血是从自己掌心流下的。
他松开了琴弦，弦上已沾满了血。他攥得太紧，把自己割伤了。醉花阴最漂亮的女人曾说，他该好好养着这双手——该弹琴的，该吹笛的，可怎么就做了这种脏事？“这杯毒酒你自己喝了，也就不负醉花阴这些年的恩义……”那好像都是很久以前的事了，他怎么还记得。
而抬起头的那一刻，那张溅血的脸又要隐去了。不能，不能这般。他不能忘的。若他都忘记恨了，这世上还有谁会记得？

“你真要去杀他？就你一人？你疯了？”那个和他一样孤身一人的女子少见地瞪大眼睛问他。
他没回答，只是把掌心的血轻轻抹向脖颈，就像画出一条上吊的红绳。
en:
Again and again, Han Wei traced that man's visage in his mind.
A dragon robe drenched in blood. City gates thrown wide. The man came riding through on horseback, each hoofbeat pressing a crescent moon of blood into the earth, one after another, trampling over loyalty and treachery, love and hatred, all the way to the Golden Throne Hall. And those blood-red crescents would begin to curve into a smile, a grin about to split open and swallow the world whole: the heads of grown men, the flatbreads clutched in the hands of women and children. Every time, it ended this way.
Try as he might, he could not picture that face unsullied by blood. Yes, blood. His father's blood. His mother's blood. The blood of the entire Han clan.
And as he lingered on the thought, blood began to trickle from the corner of that face's eye in the vision before him, winding down in a long red thread. That man was crying? How could he cry? He was emperor now. His name would be written into the chronicles for ages to come. What did he have to weep for?

Then pain jolted him back. Ah, the blood was flowing from his own palm.
He released the guqin string. It was already slick with red. He had gripped it so hard that it had cut into his palm. The most beautiful woman in Velvet Shade had once told him he ought to cherish these hands, hands made for the guqin, for the flute. How had they ended up sullied by work like this? "Drink this cup of poison yourself, and you'll have repaid Velvet Shade for all its kindness over the years..." It seemed like a lifetime ago, and yet he still remembered every word.
But the moment he lifted his head, that blood-streaked face was about to fade away again. No. He could not allow that. He must not forget. If even he forgot how to hate, then who in this world would remember?

"You're really going to kill him? By yourself? Are you mad?" asked the woman, another soul as solitary as he was, her eyes wide with a rare flash of shock.
He did not answer. He only took the blood from his palm and drew it lightly across his throat, tracing a crimson line like a noose.

延广真欲救天下尔？欲献技于上而复得宠也！
上欲救天下尔？称孙于契丹，不取利、妄起衅，搏名青史也！
墨者真欲救天下尔？以奇技淫巧能救天下，世所未闻也！

今且观之，皆搏名利之跳梁丑，而戏你我小民而已。国策？民策？天下策？于你何益？于我何益？如梦呓，作笑谈。
en:
A Mohist arrived from the North, claiming to possess a grand strategy to save the world. Hearing of this, Jing Yanguang lavishly invited him into his estate.

At first, the Mohist carried himself with arrogance, proposing several schemes to Guang. None were accepted, and he prepared to leave. Yanguang then made a wager: if the Mohist could recreate the legendary Deheng's Spectacle Puppet and have it run for ten days without stopping, his strategy would be adopted. The Mohist agreed and completed the work in a month. The mechanism ran for nine days without pause, but on the tenth day, when the Mohist asked for funds to repair the Yellow River canals, Yanguang laughed heartily. He led the Mohist to see the puppet; its gears had jammed, and the machine had collapsed. Bewildered, the Mohist inspected it, only to find a single wooden peg that did not fit the design. Yanguang made another wager: if the Mohist could drink a hundred jars of wine within the estate, his strategy would be accepted.

What a laughable farce! I wonder, did that Mohist manage to drain all one hundred jars?

Did Yanguang truly wish to save the world? He merely sought to present a novelty to the Emperor to regain royal favor!

Did the Emperor truly wish to save the world? Calling himself a "grandson" to the Khitans, gaining no real advantage yet recklessly provoking a war, all just to make a name in history!

Did the Mohist truly wish to save the world? The idea that clever trinkets and mechanics can save the world is unheard of!

Looking back, they were little more than liars driven by fame and profit, putting on an elaborate performance to deceive the commoners. National strategy? People's welfare? World salvation? What good does it do you? What good does it do me? It is all just a joke, like ramblings of a dream.

zh:
抢哥：

我这人嘴笨，以前你总怨我不吭声。
如今你蹲牢子，我想说话也找不到人，心里忽然好些话，索性一气写下。

其实，二十年前我没跑，不是因为讲义气，是那些娃子拉帮结派都有靠山，就我和谁都说不上话，我怕被你揍，所以愣在原地。

劫道那天我没跑，也不是因为讲义气，是我从未听过将死之人的声音，吓得我不敢动弹，所以愣在原地。

你让我守财那天我没跑，更不是因为讲义气，是我想起你我二人过去种种和渺茫的以后，一下就说不出话来了，所以愣在原地。

从前，你总嚷着教我功夫，要带我闯江湖，可我连招式都记不全，一再推脱。

后来，你为我出头背上命案，我们不得不闯，可逃到半路又被偷去全副盘缠……

那一刻我就知道，你我二人，一个莽，一个愣，真像这乱世里的飞蚊，明明想要活，偏撞到死路上。

你总说我一生就是一个愣字，那这十年，我索性就愣给你看。
这一次，你就当我是讲义气吧。

……胡言乱语写了这么多，也是白写。
反正你都不认得字，等你见着这封信，我就说是在回忆我俩儿时的快乐日子吧。
en:
Qiang,

I've never been good with words. You used to complain about it all the time, always saying I never spoke up.
Now that you're behind bars, there's no one left to talk to. All of a sudden I've got plenty to say, so I might as well write it all down.

Twenty years ago, the day I didn't run.It wasn't because I had honor. Those kids all had their own crews and backers, and I had none. I was afraid you'd beat me, so I just froze where I stood.
The day of the robbery, I didn't run either. Not out of honor. I'd never heard what a dying man sounds like. It scared me stiff, and I couldn't move, so I just froze there again.
The day you told me to guard the money, I still didn't run. That wasn't honor either. I thought about everything we'd been through, and about how little of a future we ever had, and the words just wouldn't come. So I froze there.

You were always trying to teach me to fight, always talking about how we'd make our way through the jianghu together. But I could never even remember the moves. I kept putting it off and making excuses.
Then you fought for me and took a life for it. We had no choice but to run. And halfway there we got robbed of every last coin we had.
That's when I knew it. One of us was reckless, the other was uselessly stuck. Two gnats in a world gone mad, trying to live and still slamming straight into a dead end.

You always said my whole life could be summed up in one word: "stuck." Fine. For the past ten years, I've stayed stuck for you.

This time, you can say it was honor.

...Look at all this. I'm rambling on and it's all for nothing anyway. You can't even read.
When this letter reaches you, I'll just say I was writing about the good old days when we were kids.
Daddy—!

zh:
师傅说，南方的草，很难在北方活。橘生淮南则为橘，生于淮北则为枳，满山野疯长的茱萸到了此地，也难免枯萎干瘪，成了北地的“枯茱萸”。虽不如南方那般长得旺盛，好歹扎了根，喘了气。朱鱼用它入药，竟还能治些轻微的寒症，可朱鱼已救不了自己。朝生暮落花的毒，不知何时所染，早成附骨之蛆，在师傅蹙眉的那一刻，朱鱼便知晓了一切，也想好了一切。朱鱼没有告诉冯夷，咸鱼郎最是狠戾，恐生大乱，洪水欲来，一人之命无足轻重，毕竟河伯想保的，是全城的命。

人有了无惧苍天的胆魄，便才有资格，成这万古一人的“河伯”。瓠子堤破，漫天皆是滔滔浊浪时，朱鱼第一次觉得，自己有了河伯的胆魄。朝生暮落之毒，既缓以寒气蚀骨，亦可催动寒毒，成就昙花一现的“朝生暮落”。龙蛟帮众从未见过那样的朱帮主，谈笑慷慨，挥刀断浪，驭龙援弛，如同神降，龙蛟帮的纤歌，终于在朱鱼高亢而坚定的呼喊下再一次响起：

“天上这星多呦喂，月不明——”
“河里这鱼多呦喂，水不清——”
“地上这人多呦喂，气不宁——”
“这黄河不枯呦喂，世不平——”

那是朱鱼最后的歌声。
en:
Master said that grass from the south could barely survive in the north. Oranges grown south of the Huai River are sweet oranges; those grown north become bitter trifoliate oranges. The dogwood that ran wild all over the mountains in the south would inevitably wither and shrink here, becoming "Dried Dogwood Berry" of the north. Though not as lush as in the south, it at least took root and breathed. Zhu Yu used it as medicine and surprisingly cured some mild colds, but she couldn't save herself. She had been poisoned by the Dawn-to-Dusk, though she knew not when. The poison had long festered like maggots clinging to bone. The moment Master frowned, Zhu Yu understood everything and had already made up her mind. She didn't tell Feng Yi. That salted fish scoundrel was ruthless; she feared it would spark great chaos. A flood was imminent, and one life was insignificant. After all, what River Deity wanted to protect was the lives of the entire city. 

Only one who possesses the courage to defy heaven is worthy of becoming that singular "River Deity" for all ages. When the Huzi Dike broke and turbid waves filled the sky, Zhu Yu felt, for the first time, that she possessed the River Deity's courage. The Dawn-to-Dusk poison, which slowly eroded the bones with cold, could also be spurred to create a brief, dazzling "bloom." The Dragon Hall had never seen Leader Zhu like this, generous in speech and laughter, cleaving waves with her blade, commanding dragons to aid and relax, as if a god had descended. The sect's hauling song finally rang out once more under Zhu Yu's resolute cry: 

"So many stars in the sky, oh hey, the moon is dim..." 
"So many fish in the river, oh hey, the water is murky..." 
"So many people on the earth, oh hey, the air is uneasy..." 
"This Yellow River never dries, oh hey, the world is unjust..." 

That was Zhu Yu's final song.

zh:
弟子简行之，已抵岱山脚下，投宿于时来客栈。同行宿客共八人，外加掌柜一人。
是夜漫天飞雪，又有闷雷隐隐。时当隆冬，天象之异，莫此为甚。江湖相传“千雷响，魔头出”，恐所言非虚。
据馆中载，那魔头原属道真一脉。安史之乱后，此脉式微，早已湮没无闻。
却不知那蓝何，是从何处得了道真传承？有言其假死脱身，今已至岱山。是觊觎那人功法？还是要助其出山，搅出一番事来？
弟子本为追查馆中所传“梅花信”。既至此地，决意候魔头出山，当面亲询，以了此案。
谨以目之所见，追录当日之实；继以道之所在，追未解之谜。倘有变故——
en:
I, Jian Xingzhi, have arrived at the foot of Mount Tai and taken a room at the Fortune's Favor Inn. There are eight other guests, plus the innkeeper.
Snow fills the sky, and heavy thunder grumbles. Strange weather for deep winter. "The fiend walks free to a thousand thunders' roar," some say. I fear that may be more than rumor.
According to our records, the fiend was of the Daozhen lineage. After the An Lushan Rebellion, the line faded into obscurity.
But how did Lan He acquire the Daozhen legacy? Rumor has it that he faked his death and is now at Mount Tai. Does he want the fiend's power? Or to free her, and loose her upon the world?
I came to investigate the "Plum Blossom Letter". As I am already here, I shall wait for the fiend to emerge, to question her myself and close this case.
Let this be a record of the truth of this day. I will follow this mystery's path to its end. Should anything befall...

zh: 采菊酿酒是重阳历史最悠久的传统之一。汉代《西京杂记》介绍了菊花酒的酿制方法，“菊花舒时，并采茎叶，杂黍为酿之，至来年九月九日始熟，就饮焉，故谓之菊花酒。”到了唐朝，菊花酒被载入《千金要方》，认为它有“治男妇老人虚劳癖瘦，腰膝疼痛，消渴嗌干”之效。菊花酒亦成为唐宋诗人纪念重阳的意象之一，如上官婉儿诗云“帝里重阳节，香园万乘来。却邪萸入佩，献寿菊传杯。”
en: Brewing chrysanthemum wine is one of the oldest Double Ninth traditions. Han-era "Miscellaneous Records of the Western Capital" describes the method: "When chrysanthemums bloom, gather stems and leaves, mix with millet, and ferment until the next ninth day of the ninth month before drinking, hence called chrysanthemum wine." By the Tang, it was recorded in "Essential Formulas for Emergencies" for its health benefits. It also became a poetic motif for the festival.

zh: 算盘普及之前，古人最主要的计算工具。多用竹子、木头或兽骨制成一根根长短一致的小棍，通过纵横交错的摆放来表示不同的数字，并进行加减乘除甚至开方等复杂运算。在杭州城的各大商铺、赌坊与钱庄里，账房先生们指尖拨动算筹，运筹帷幄之间，便理清了这繁华商埠的万贯流水。

zh:
他最初的剑，是他自己的身体。

战争的星火飘落到村里，便是一场灭顶的大火。
人们张皇逃窜，唯有他还记得，姐姐还独自在家里。
门栓对一个孩子来说，太沉了。
于是他头一回生出了一个愿望——想要一把剑。
老天爷当然不会天降一把剑，
于是，他只得用自己的身体，生生撞断了门栓。
他用烙铁一样滚烫的手抓住姐姐，不顾一切地向前跑去。

他的第二把剑，是一根破树枝。

姐姐很少回应他的话，但是他知道姐姐在听。
他和姐姐讲述自己的愿望：想要一把剑——
姐姐，剑，就是很长、很尖，可以护人的东西！
于是改日，姐姐便递了一根格外直而尖的树枝给他，
他欢喜得睡觉都抱着这把“剑”。
直至那日，不知姐姐说了什么得罪了一同辗转流亡的村民，
他们群起而攻之，袒露自己的心声：
“这么一个傻子，还总是带着她做什么！”
“话也不会说，看着也活不长，早晚给狼做口粮！”
他护在姐姐身前，举起手中的剑朝向众人：“我永不会丢下她！”

后来，他被母亲青领入山，拜入她的门下后，青教他剑法，二人以战代教，活活折断了四十九柄剑。
父亲鸦看着直摇头，遂以青金石造双剑，他与姐姐，一人一把。
他无比珍惜，当着父母姐姐面前指天誓日：“定当珍爱，剑在人在！”
母亲照着他的脑袋就是一下：“什么剑在人在，本末倒置！剑，是护人之物！”
可惜，事与愿违。
在那场灭顶的大火中，凝结墨家心血的飞天城，也不过如破茅屋一般，分崩离析。
他用烙铁一样滚烫的手抓着姐姐，不顾一切向前跑，但是这一次，火比他更快。
于是，他第一次食言，他将姐姐丢了出去。
紧接着，是第二次食言，父亲赠予的剑，先他一步在爆炸中断裂。
……
在漫长的黑暗与煎熬中，他艰难睁开眼睛，做了一个决定。
他最后的剑，是他自己的身体。
en:
His first sword was his own flesh and bone.
When the sparks of war descended upon the village, they kindled an all-consuming inferno.
In the frantic flight of the masses, he alone remembered his sister, left solitary within their home.
The door bolt was far too heavy for a mere child.
And so, for the first time, a desire took root in him, the longing for a sword.
Heavens, of course, would not grant a sword from the void.
Thus, he used his own body, shattering the bolt with the raw force of his frame.
With hands as searing as branding irons, he seized his sister and plunged forward in a reckless sprint.
His second sword was a withered branch.
His sister seldom replied, yet he knew his words reached her.
He shared his heart's desire with her: he wanted a sword.
"Sister, a sword is long and sharp, a thing to keep people safe!"
Thus, on another day, she brought him a branch, one exceptionally straight and keen.
So great was his joy that he slept with his "sword" clutched to his chest.
Until that day, when some word of hers, no one knew what, offended the villagers who shared their exile.
They rose as one against her, baring the malice in their hearts:
"What use is there in dragging such a fool along!"
"Mute and frail as she is, she won't last long. Better she becomes fodder for the wolves!"
He stood fast before her, leveling his wooden sword at the crowd. "I will never forsake her!"
Later, Mother Halcyon led him into the mountains to study under her. In their relentless sparring, they shattered forty-nine blades.
Raven, the father, watched with a sigh and a shake of his head. He eventually forged twin blades of Lapis Lazuli, one for him and one for his sister.
He cherished it beyond all else. Before his kin, he swore a solemn oath: "I shall treasure it with my life. While the sword remains, so shall I!"
Mother gave his head a sharp rap. "What 'life for a sword'? You've put the cart before the horse! A sword is but a tool to protect people!"
Alas, fate willed otherwise.
In that catastrophic inferno, even the Skyward City, the crowning achievement of the Mohist, was shattered like a derelict hut.
With hands searing like brands, he gripped his sister and fled headlong, but this time, the flames outpaced him.
Thus, he broke his first vow: he cast his sister away from the heat.
Soon followed the second: his father's gift, the sword, broke in the blast before he could fall.
...
Amidst the enduring darkness and agony, he struggled to open his eyes and reached a final decision.
His final sword would be his own flesh.

zh: 《周易》成于殷周至战国间，分经、传两部。经部以八卦为基，重为六十四卦，每卦系以卦辞、爻辞，相传伏羲画八卦，文王作卦辞，周公作爻辞，本为卜筮之书。传部共十篇，称“十翼”，含彖、象、系辞、文言、说卦、序卦、杂卦诸篇，相传为孔子所作，旨在阐发阴阳消长、天人变化之理。汉代立于学官，居五经之首。魏王弼以老庄解易，扫除象数，开义理一派；唐孔颖达奉诏修《周易正义》，定为官学取士之本。历代推为“群经之首，大道之源”，其象数与义理二途，既为卜筮推算之用，亦成士大夫安身立命之学。
en: The Book of Changes was composed between the Yin-Zhou and Warring States periods, and is divided into two parts: the Canon and the Commentaries. The Canon takes the Eight Trigrams as its foundation, doubled into sixty-four Hexagrams, each accompanied by a Hexagram statement and line statements. It is said that Fu Xi drew the Eight Trigrams, King Wen composed the Hexagram statements, and the Duke of Zhou composed the line statements. The work thus originated as a book of divination. The Commentaries comprise ten chapters, known as the "Ten Wings," containing such pieces as the Tuan, the Xiang, the Appended Statements, the Refined Words, the Explanation of the Trigrams, the Sequence of Hexagrams, and the Miscellaneous Hexagrams. These are said to have been written by Confucius, with the aim of expounding the principles of the waxing and waning of yin and yang, and the transformations between Heaven and Man. In the Han dynasty, it was enshrined among the official academies, standing first among the Five Classics. In the Wei dynasty, Wang Bi interpreted the Book of Changes through the thought of Laozi and Zhuangzi, setting aside the Images and Numbers school and founding the Righteousness and Principle school. In the Tang, Kong Yingda received an imperial decree to compile the Correct Meaning of the Book of Changes, which was established as the foundation for official examinations. Every age has extolled it as "the foremost of all classics, the source of the Great Way." Its twin paths of Images and Numbers on one hand, and Righteousness and Principle on the other, serving both as tools of divination and as the lifelong learning of scholars and gentlemen alike.
Fo Bao Shi

zh:
好侄儿：
你父亲病逝一事，我们都很伤心，望你节哀，早日振作起来，重整商队。
遥想当年，你父亲带着我们商队的一群兄弟，一遍遍地拜访藤王村,和村民共谋复业之事……可惜始终没能重振藤王美酒昔日盛名。
你父亲这些年始终不肯荒废玉露台这条赔钱的商路……兄弟们嘴上抱怨，但心里都割舍不下村中的几位守藤老人。
如今你父亲先一步去了，我和你的几位叔叔年纪也大了……我们商量了一晚上，决定采纳大家的意见，以后不再走这条道了。
虽然这些年战乱不断，但天下终会重归太平……届时，藤王之名必将传遍四海！
一定会有那么一天的。
en:
Good nephew,

We're gutted by the news about your father. Mourn him, but then you need to get back on your feet and take charge of the caravan.

I can still picture him, dragging us brothers out to Kingvine Village over and over, trying to get things going with the locals... A damn shame he never saw the Kingvine Wine get its name back.

He was stubborn, your father. Kept that Cleardew Terrace route open all these years, even though it was a money pit. We complained, sure, but none of us had the heart to turn our backs on the old folks still tending the vines there.

Well, he's gone now, and the rest of us aren't getting any younger. We debated all night and we've made a decision—we're done with that route. We can't afford it anymore.

These wars won't last forever. The world will find peace again... And when it does, everyone will know the name Kingvine Wine!

That day is coming. You can bet on it.

en:
To the Faction Master:
Heavy rainstorms have raged for ten consecutive days. Mountain floods have destroyed several villages, and waves of displaced people have surged to the outskirts of Hidden Mountain, suffering from hunger and cold. We have been busy treating them alongside the senior Mohist members. Though we have exhausted all our efforts, our strength is lacking, and we must seek further methods of assistance. We have thought of two approaches but dare not act on our own authority, so we ask the Faction Master to make the final decision.
The first is to raise funds. Using the Faction Master's prestige, we can call upon all sides for charitable donations. Once the money is collected, we will uniformly purchase grain, rice, clothes, and blankets to distribute everywhere.
The second is to open the granaries. We can boil porridge and hand out flatbread to resolve their immediate starvation.
Please instruct us on which path to choose as soon as possible.

It has thirty-six scales along each side of its spine, each bearing a small black dot, and its colors include red, white, and yellow." China's earliest fish farming manual, Fan Li's Fish Farming Classic, also records methods for raising carp.

zh:
长风万里，终度玉门。你来到了那座巍峨的城关之下。此刻，它已不是难以越过的雄关天堑，而是春风西行的驿站。在旌旗飘扬的风沙里，你仿佛又一次看到了那位白头将军，正站在城墙之上，远眺东方。他眼里所见，心中所念，口中所说的皆为一句话：长安，如今可好？你踌躇半晌，开口道……
#Y【长安已不在了。】你决定说出实话——长安已经陷落，如今天下最繁华之处是开封城。但人们仍念着长安，念着昔日的盛景与安宁。#E
听闻你的回答，将军颔首沉吟，眼中似有热泪。“长安……是个很好，很好的地方。”将军浑厚苍凉的嗓音里带着怀念，也带着慨然。满城少年变白发，手中的锋镞依然，归唐之心依然。城中传来阵阵鼓声，似有千军万马列阵。你听不清他们口中呼喊的名字，但你知道，那是千万乡音汇成的两个字——长安。
en:
The endless winds travel thousands of miles, finally passing through Jade Gate Pass. You arrive beneath that towering fortress. It is no longer an impassable stronghold, but a waystation for the spring breeze journeying west. In the windblown sand, with banners snapping overhead, you seem to glimpse the white-haired general once more, standing atop the wall and gazing east. What he sees in his eyes, holds in his heart, and speaks on his lips all resolve into a single refrain: "How fares Chang'an now?" You hesitate for a long while and say...
#Y[Chang'an is gone.] You decide to tell the truth: Chang'an has already fallen, and the most flourishing city in the world today is Kaifeng. Yet people still miss Chang'an, remembering its past grandeur and peace.#E
Hearing your answer, the general nods in silent thought, tears seemingly welling in his eyes. "Chang'an... is a very, very fine place." The general's deep and desolate voice carries a sense of nostalgia, as well as a profound sorrow. The youths of the city have turned white-haired, yet the weapons in their hands remain sharp, as does their resolve to return to the Tang. From within the city comes the rolling beat of drums, as if an army of thousands were falling into formation. You cannot clearly hear the name they cry, but you know it is a single name formed by thousands of homesick voices: Chang'an.

第六十一回·横四海兮焉穷

上回说到，云中君为世人一一拨去迷雾，将知识交与大家。但因为缁尘恶人和天灾的阻挠，云中君失去了她心爱的弟子们；而云中君自己也遭到时岁反噬，失去了她最好的搭档詹老，还失去了星子的指引。
但这并不是云中君的结局！
后来，在又黑又暗的天陉深处，世人终于找到了奄奄一息的云中君。大家没有忘记她的辛劳，也十分感念她的付出，便同心协力将四散的星子碎片重新拼合起来，在天陉上为云中君点亮了成百上千盏星灯。
云中君终于又看见了！
她依着星光走啊走，一路行到了尽头……那里有一片浩瀚无垠的蒲公草花海，正是数十年前她亲手植下的。在花海里，她遇见了一个特别懂事的小女孩。小女孩从她的手里接过了那绚丽但沉重的星子披风，说：
“今后的旅途，就由我来带领云大侠吧。我们一起乘风飞到天上去，将星子分给每一个人。”

全传终。
en:
Part LXI: Across the Four Seas, Where Could There Be an End

Last time, we told how Lord of Clouds cleared the mists away for the people one by one and placed knowledge in their hands. Yet because of the schemes of wicked men and the blows of natural disaster, she lost the disciples she had treasured most dearly. And she herself, struck by the backlash of time, lost Elder Zhan, her finest companion, and with him the guidance of the stars.
But this was not the end of Lord of Clouds.
Later, in the deepest reaches of the Heaven's Threshold, black and lightless, the people at last found her, barely clinging to life. They had not forgotten her hardships, and they deeply cherished all she had done for them. So with one heart, they gathered the scattered fragments of the stars and pieced them back together, lighting hundreds upon thousands of star lamps along the Heaven's Threshold for her.
At last, Lord of Clouds could see again.
Following the starlight, she walked on and on, all the way to the very end... There, she found a vast sea of dandelions, planted by her own hand decades before. There, she met a little girl, bright and thoughtful beyond her years. From Lord of Clouds' hands, the girl took up the radiant yet weighty starry mantle and said:
"From here on, let me lead the way. Together, we'll ride the wind into the heavens and share the stars with everyone."

Thus ends the tale.
Yun Shuang

若是听得顺耳，它便汪汪高歌，摇尾转圈以示嘉奖。
不慎弹错了一个音，妮妮也会嗷一声惨叫，四脚朝天装作气绝，令奏乐者羞愧难当。
渐渐地，能让妮妮“汪”上一声，竟成了乐官们炫耀实力的资本。
大家甚至为了公平竞艺定下铁则：谁也不许带肉干感贿赂考官！
长春节佳节，庆寿殿献艺大演在即，教坊乐师和乐官摩拳擦掌。
无需多言，他们将迎来妮妮最严格的品评。
en:
Gou Di is a rough-and-ready guard, but the little dog it picked up, Nini, is an absolute "connoisseur."

Nini doesn't care for meat buns. It would rather listen to music. Whenever the musicians rehearse, it shows up to "audit" the performance.

If it likes what it hears, it sings along with happy barks, tail wagging as it spins in circles. But hit a wrong note and Nini will let out a dramatic howl, flop onto its back with all four paws in the air, and play dead on the spot. The performers never recover from the shame.

Over time, earning even a single approving "woof" from Nini became something the musicians bragged about. For fairness, they even laid down a hard rule: no one is allowed to bribe the judge with dried meat.

Now the Changchun Festival is near, and a grand show at Qingshou Hall is about to begin. The troupe is ready.
No further explanation needed. Nini's strictest judging is about to start.

zh:
“今夜，那只鸟儿还会来吗？”
亥时一刻，月上枝头。沈玉倚在窗边，暗自思量。
自打那夜的“意外”后，萧史便如同鸟儿一般，闯入她的世界，扰乱了她波澜不惊的生活。
每夜，他都会带些小玩意来。叽叽喳喳的，讲一些她从不知晓的市井烟火，江湖快意。
沈玉听着，仿佛自己变成了鸟儿，穿梭在人群中，她的心随着故事，头一次这么自由。
或许，在他人看来，她永远是那恰到好处，微笑着的沈家大小姐，她也知晓如何让大家喜欢。但只有在一个人时，她才能放下笑脸，做回自己。但“自己”本应该是怎样的呢？

“今夜，他不会来了吧……”
亥时三刻，月悬天幕。沈玉倚在窗边，思绪飘远。
会不会，自己每次的拒绝……终于让他失去了耐心？
但……若不拒绝，一旦被父亲发现，这唯一的自由，也就没了。
可，听闻自己那未婚夫婿……那指挥使独子马上就要回来了。这样的自由日子，又还能持续多久呢？
沈玉自知无法挣脱压在自己身上的职责与期许，无法逃离被规定的命运。这些从出生就牢牢印在了她身上。过着优渥的生活，或许就要舍弃一些东西吧。但在大家都睡着的深夜，她总是会踌躇难眠。

“今夜，便不给他开窗了吧。”
亥时六刻，月挂中天。窗外，响起了熟悉的声音，又是萧史用笛子学那鸟叫声。
“他来了。”
真不知道，这是在哪儿学的奇怪技法。沈玉不自知的笑了起来。
她时不时也会想，自己这唯一一次的打破礼数，真的是对的吗？顺从自己的内心，是被允许的吗？但在听到鸟声的那一刻，踌躇、犹豫、挣扎一瞬间都散去了。
望着紧闭的窗扉，她叹了一口气……

今夜的沈玉，依旧推开了那扇窗。
en:
"Will the bird come tonight?"
As the moon hung low among the branches and the household slept, Shen Yu lingered by the window, her thoughts wandering. Ever since that night's unexpected encounter, Xiao Shi had flitted into her world like a restless bird, unsettling the calm of her well-ordered life. Night after night, he brought small trinkets and stories, chattering about bustling streets and the wild freedom of the jianghu—worlds she'd never known.

Listening to him, Shen Yu felt as if she too had grown wings, drifting through crowds, her heart lighter and freer than it had ever been. To everyone else, she was still the impeccably poised Miss Shen—smiling, gracious, unfailingly charming. She knew exactly how to win people's affection. But only in solitude could she let her guard down and be herself. Yet what did "herself" truly mean?

"Tonight... he won't come, will he?"
As the night deepened and the moon climbed higher, Shen Yu lingered at the window, her thoughts drifting. Had her repeated refusals finally worn him down? Yet if she never pushed him away, her one sliver of freedom would vanish the moment her father found out. Worse, her betrothed—the commander's only son—would soon return. How many nights like this remained?

Shen Yu knew she could never escape the duties and expectations pressed upon her from birth, nor the fate carved by her family's name. A life of privilege demanded its sacrifices. Yet in the silent hours, as the household slept, doubt gnawed at her.

"Tonight, I won't open the window."
As the moon reached its zenith, a familiar sound echoed outside—Xiao Shi mimicking bird calls on his flute.
"He came."
Where had he learned such a strange trick? Shen Yu couldn't help but smile. She often wondered if breaking the rules just this once was truly right. Was following her heart ever allowed? Yet at the sound of his flute, all her hesitation melted away.

She gazed at the tightly shut window and sighed... yet, in the end, she reached out and opened it.

zh:
蒋沧海的乐声是村里节庆的信号。
只要听到海边从远及近的乐声，孩子们就会欢呼着跑向他们的“潮师父”。
木马灵巧，花枪如龙，蒋沧海鼓起腮帮，吹着欢乐的曲调，迈向他扎根的村子。人们在他的乐声中起舞，欢笑，庆祝着丰收与佳节。
他的戏法和乐声，带给村里人很多快乐。

但蒋沧海年轻时也曾吹过两次哀乐。
第一次，是他告别师父祝丑公之前。
师父在一群卖艺的孩子中一眼看中他的天赋，拐了他入门传授武功。
师父对他很好，永远都笑呵呵的。可蒋沧海还是惦记着村里一年一度的灯会，还有村里没修好的栈桥。
几年过去了，师父决定放他离开，只是需要他陪自己去参加一场葬礼。
那是师父故人的葬礼。听说，他们曾一起做了件偷天换日的大事。后来这位故人开了个古玩店，做着不咸不淡的生意。
蒋沧海一开始不信。师父怎么看都是个普通的古怪老头，骗骗孩子就罢了，怎么会做过那等掉脑袋的大事?
到了葬礼上，蒋沧海信了——他吹起哀挽的歌，却被师父拍了脑袋。
“喜事啊！傻徒弟，吹个乐呵的！”那位“逝者”正乐呵呵地坐在棺椁前，拉着师父肆意大笑，鼓盆作歌。
蒋沧海不懂，但他吹得很尽兴。原来，哀歌也可以变作喜乐。他也笑了，吹得更卖力，直到眼前都浮现了金色的星尘。
师父给了蒋沧海了一大笔钱，随后便追着他的老友大笑离去。掂量着钱袋子，蒋沧海咧开嘴笑得开心。要去镇子里买多多的风筝和蜜糖，还要帮村里把栈桥修好，他想。

第二次，是他回到村子里的时候。
原本应该缠绕花环的断桥插满暗淡的白花，本应高高挑起的红灯笼变作了灵幡。
收留他的孙婆婆，昨晚去了滩涂，再也没回来。
村里人断断续续的言语在耳边回响。他才知道这些年里，孙婆婆一直在找自己。
潮水声远远传来，仿佛是婆婆担心的呜咽。

他不能让婆婆哭着走，他要让婆婆笑着回到大海。于是他甩干脸上的泪水，爬上了高跷木马。
“哗啦啦的黄河水哎——”蒋沧海吹响了最激昂的戏乐，迈着奔马似的舞步，耍起花枪，赴约了盛大的庆典。
原来，喜乐也可以变作哀歌。乡亲们都哭了，他吹得更卖力，直到眼前再次浮现了金色的星尘。

后来，蒋沧海搬到了海边，换了个“观潮客”的称号。他守着潮滩，望着大海，也迈着舞步，吹着曲子。
他还是会回到村子里参加庆典，为村里人送来新鲜的鱼虾。
每天看着海潮和日出的人，心里也比别人亮堂。
他要用戏法和乐曲，为大家带去更多的欢笑，或是泪水。
在欢笑与泪水共舞的时刻，他好像又回到了过去的日子。
师父，婆婆，乡亲们，都合在一处为自己鼓掌。
en:
Jiang Canghai's music served as the village's signal for festivities.
Whenever the children heard the melodies drifting closer from the seashore, they would cheer and run toward their "Master of the Tides." Riding a nimble wooden horse and wielding a floral spear like a dragon, Jiang Canghai would puff his cheeks, blow a joyous tune, and stride toward the village where he had put down roots. Amidst his music, the people would dance, laugh, and celebrate the bountiful harvest and auspicious holidays. His myriad tricks and melodies brought boundless joy to the villagers.
Yet, in his youth, Jiang Canghai had also played the dirge on two occasions.
The first time was before he bid farewell to his master, Zhu Chougong. His master had spotted his talent at a glance among a group of child street performers, whisking him away to teach him martial arts. The master treated him exceedingly well, always wearing a genial smile. Still, Jiang Canghai missed the annual lantern festival in his village and the unfinished wooden pier back home. After several years passed, the master decided to let him go, asking only that the boy accompany him to a funeral.
It was the funeral of an old friend of the master. It was said that the two of them had once pulled off an earth-shattering endeavor that could fool the world. Later, this friend opened an antique shop mediocre in every way. Jiang Canghai did not believe it at first. In every respect, his master seemed like nothing more than an eccentric old man; tricking children was one thing, but how could he have partaken in a capital crime?
Upon arriving at the funeral, Jiang Canghai finally believed. He began to play a sorrowful elegy, only to receive a gentle smack on the head from his master.
"This is a joyous occasion! You silly disciple, play something cheerful!" The "deceased" was sitting merrily before his own coffin, pulling the master into boisterous laughter, beating a basin and singing a song of transcendence.
Jiang Canghai did not understand, but he played to his heart's content. So, an elegy could also become a melody of joy. He smiled too, blowing his instrument with even greater fervor, until golden stardust danced before his eyes.
The master gave Jiang Canghai a substantial sum of money, then chased after his old friend, departing with a hearty laugh. Weighing the heavy coin pouch in his hand, Jiang Canghai broke into a wide, radiant smile. He thought of going to the town to buy plenty of kites and honey candies, and of helping the village repair that broken pier.
The second time was when he returned to his village.
The broken bridge, which should have been woven with festive garlands, was now planted with bleak white flowers; the red lanterns that should have hung high were replaced by funeral banners. Granny Sun, who had once taken him in, had gone to the tidal flats the night before and never returned. The fragmented whispers of the villagers echoed in his ears. Only then did he realize that all these years, Granny Sun had been tirelessly searching for him. The sound of the tide drifted from afar, sounding just like the old woman's worried weeping.
He could not let Granny Sun depart in tears; he had to let her return to the sea with a smile. Thus, he shook the tears from his face and climbed onto his stilted wooden horse.
"Ha! Hear the roar of the Yellow River!" Jiang Canghai blew the most impassioned theatrical tune. Marching with the vigorous steps of a galloping steed, he twirled his floral spear, honoring his appointment at a grand celebration.
Thus, a melody of joy could also become an elegy. The villagers all wept, yet he played with even greater fervor, until the golden stardust once again danced before his eyes.
Later, Jiang Canghai moved to the seaside and took up the moniker of "Tidewatcher." He guarded the tidal flats, gazing at the ocean, still dancing his steps and playing his tunes. He would still return to the village to join the festivities, bringing fresh fish and shrimp to the locals. He believed that those who watched the tide and the sunrise every day held a brighter light in their hearts than others. He would use his tricks and melodies to bring everyone more laughter, or perhaps tears.
In those moments where laughter and tears danced together, he felt as though he had returned to the days of old. His master, Granny Sun, and the villagers were all gathered in one place, applauding for him.

en:
My dear disciple Mingqiong,
I was gravely wounded hunting down the last of the Xuanyuan Cult, and I'm afraid this is where my path ends. As I look back on a life well spent, my only thought is of you. When I found you in a mass grave, you couldn't even speak then, yet your tiny hands already gripped a blade. I feared the demon in your heart would swallow you whole... But after you joined the Lone Cloud, I watched you grow, year by year, into the light. It has been my greatest comfort.
Do you know the meaning of your name, Mingqiong? Light and shadow are born of each other. You were born into the darkness, but I wished for you to become the light that pierces the vault of heaven. The world will always swing between light and dark. May you always hold fast to the light within you, and never let hatred cloud your sight.

Wanderer! We heard you hail from Qinghe, which makes us practically neighbors! Folks up in Qinghe love their meat stew, and we in Qingzhou are just as crazy about it. Anyone who appreciates a good bowl of meat stew is family in our book! And since you're family, we couldn't let you travel all this way without giving you a proper welcome gift.
We don't have any fancy treasures, so we all pitched in and put together this journal! Little Master Yang mentioned that scholars out there carry something similar, some fancy book they call "Good Times Chronicles." We took his idea, tacked on a few extra pages of our own, and decided to call it the "Qingzhou Mountain Travelogue."
Whenever you catch a breathtaking view or run into something fun on the road, jot it down here. And when your feet get tired, you can flip through the pages and remember the breeze of Qingzhou, the earth of this land, and all of us cheering you on!

zh:
乾祐三年 十二月
郭留守入城后，开封大乱。沈义仁大哥率我等部众妻小遁入山林，躲避搜捕。贺二叫得最凶，他不愿眼前的富贵转头成空，吵着要杀回城中。我心知此劫难渡，只望众人平安。

乾祐四年 正月
大乱引发大饥，饿殍流离遍野。城内尚且如此，何况寒冬山野？飞豹与铁猛已握不住刀了，贺二也早就不再叫骂，他盯着妇孺的眼神令人发毛。
再找不到粮食我们都得死。不用等他人来剿灭我们，我们就会死！

乾祐四年 二月
郑氏当真尚有余粮！
贺二已经跟着大哥冲杀了过去，但我们怎能用无辜者的命，换自己的命…？
我不愿往，直到看到秉节兄弟的女儿，那小姑娘刚出生没几日就生生被饿到断气。秉节媳妇不肯承认眼前的事实，她自己都饿的瘦骨嶙峋、双腿肿胀，却还死死抱着孩子，她说：“惜惜乖，再坚持一会，就有米汤吃了。”
我看着惜惜即将断气的姐姐，握紧了手中的枪。

乾祐四年 三月
秉节竟然偷偷留了个活口！除了青溪侠客救下的郑氏，竟然还有幸存者！
那是个不过月余的女婴，秉节偷偷留下了她。我在看到秉节媳妇抱着孩子，唤她“希希”，并给她喂米汤的时候，就明白了情由。
我想办法帮他们瞒过了贺二，得让这孩子活下去，她必须活下去！
……
……

显德元年 正月
寒菌已经爬满了北山。
村里人都在议论中毒郑氏的东渡自殉。沈义伦最愤慨，他一直将郑氏的苦难归因于自己，无法接受这样的结局。
我遏止了他的悲号。不是觉得他说错了，而是担忧他的安危。
——贺二想弄死他。大哥毕竟已经故去，先兄幼弟的身份，保不了他多久了。

显德元年 二月
沈义伦失踪了！
村中人心惶惶，因为就在前几日，贺二便计划着要将老弱和不服管教者统统逐出村落，以应对愈演愈烈的毒患和饥荒！
他还要赶走秉重、秉节的媳妇丫头，铁锰的妹妹和老娘！他甚至问我讨要主宅的另半块钥匙，要拾回甲胄、重操旧业！
我不该容忍他这么久的。不应该！

显德元年 六月
尘埃落定了。
贺岳峙被迫出走后，我与留下的人约法三章，再不行流寇作为，再不抛弃老弱妇孺，努力耕种、平静生活。
开启主宅的半块钥匙亦被我锁在了暗井下面。或许许多年后我会与昭明他们坦白过往的一切，向希希和其他的达安郑氏赎过去的罪。或许... 我们能一起见到天下常平，黎民无饥的那一日？
en:
Layue, the Third Year of the Qianyou Era
After Governor Guo Liushou entered the city, Kaifeng fell into chaos. Shen Yiren led all of us into the mountains to escape the raids. He Er complained the most, furious that all our wealth could disappear overnight. He wanted to fight our way back into the city. But I knew this was a disaster we couldn't outrun. All I wished for was that our people would make it through alive.

Zhengyue, the Fourth Year of the Qianyou Era
The unrest soon turned into famine. Starving refugees and unburied dead lay everywhere in the city. How could we survive out here in the dead of winter? Some no longer had the strength to even hold a blade. And He Er... he wasn't shouting anymore. The way he looked at the women and children chilled me to the bone.
If we didn't find food soon, we'd die—enemies don't need to kill us; hunger would finish the job.

February, the Fourth Year of the Qianyou Era
The Zheng family actually still had grain!
Some had already charged in, but how could we justify taking innocent lives for ourselves? I refused to go—until I saw a baby girl starving to death. So I tightened my grip on my spear.

March, the Fourth Year of the Qianyou Era
There was another survivor: a baby girl barely a month old. One of our people hid her away. I saw a woman cradling the baby girl, feeding her rice soup, and I understood everything.
I covered it up, so He Er wouldn't find out.
This child has to live. Whatever it takes—she must survive.

Zhengyue, the First Year of the Xiande Era
The frost fungus has already spread over the northern mountain.
The villagers keep talking about Zheng's suicide. Shen Yilun is furious—he blames himself for Zheng's suffering and can't accept such a fate. I held back his grief for his safety.
He Er wants him dead. As the younger brother of the late chief, Shen will soon get trapped in danger.

February, the First Year of the Xiande Era
Shen Yilun has gone missing!
Everyone in the village is on edge. Just a few days ago, He Er planned to drive out all the old, the weak, and the rebellious to deal with the worsening poison and famine!
He even intended to send away the wives and girls of our men. He asked me for the other half of the house's key, planning to arm himself and go back to his old ways!
I shouldn't have put up with him for so long. I really shouldn't have!

June, the First Year of the Xiande Era
The dust has finally settled.
Those who stayed made a pact—no more banditry, no more abandoning the weak. We'd work the land and live in peace.
The other half of the key is now hidden beneath a secret well. Maybe, years from now, I'll confess everything and ask for forgiveness. Maybe... someday, we'll see that promise fulfilled, and at that time, no one goes hungry.
