en:
【Miscellaneous Records II, Section 21】

If a person is in mourning for their father, and before the mourning period ends, their mother dies, then when the time comes to end the mourning for the father, they wear the appropriate garments for ending that mourning. After the ceremony is complete, they return to the mourning garments for the mother. Even in the case of mourning for uncles or brothers, if it coincides with mourning for parents, when the time comes to end the mourning for uncles or brothers, they all wear the garments appropriate for ending that mourning. After the ceremony is complete, they return to the mourning garments for the parents. If it is a three-year mourning period, then after the ceremony of removing the mourning sash, the ceremonies of the one-year and two-year anniversaries are the same. If the grandfather dies, and before the one-year and two-year anniversary ceremonies, the grandson also dies, the grandson is still attached to the grandfather in the ancestral rites. If there is an encoffined body in the house, and news of a death outside arrives, one weeps for it in another room. One enters to make the offering, and after completing the offering, leaves, changes garments, and takes one's place, following the same rites as when first taking one's place. When a grand officer or officer is about to participate in a sacrifice at the ruler's court, if after having inspected the vessels for washing, a parent dies, they still participate in the sacrifice, but lodge in a separate palace. After the sacrifice, they remove their ceremonial garments, go outside the ruler's gate, weep, and then return home. Other matters follow the rites of rushing to a funeral. If they have not yet inspected the washing vessels, they send someone to report. After the messenger returns, they then weep. In the case of mourning for uncles, brothers, aunts, or sisters, if they have already received the notice of the sacrifice, they participate in it. After completing the ceremony, they go out of the ruler's gate, remove their garments, and then return home. Other matters follow the rites of rushing to a funeral. If they share the same palace, they lodge in a separate one.
Zengzi asked: "If a minister or grand officer is to act as the representative of the deceased at the ruler's sacrifice, and has received the notice, but then a death occurs within their own family requiring mourning of the kind where one wears unhemmed sackcloth, what should be done?" Confucius said: "They should go out and lodge at the ruler's palace to await the event—this is proper." Confucius also said: "When the representative of the deceased goes out wearing a leather cap or a ceremonial cap, the ministers, grand officers, and officers all descend from their carriages. The representative must bow from the carriage, and there must be someone leading in front."
During mourning for parents, if just before the sacrifice, a brother dies, the sacrifice is performed after the encoffining. If they share the same palace, then even if it is a servant or concubine who dies, the sacrifice is performed only after burial. At the sacrifice, the host ascends and descends without following the proper steps, and the attendants also do not follow the proper steps. This is also the case at the burial and the subsequent ancestral rites. From the feudal lords down to the officers, at the sacrifice of the one-year anniversary, when the host receives the cup in reply, he tastes it; the guests and brothers all sip it. At the two-year anniversary sacrifice: the host sips it, and the guests and brothers may all drink it fully. In all cases of attending a mourning sacrifice, one tells the guests to offer the food but not to eat it.
Zigong asked about mourning, and the Master said: "Reverence is the highest, grief comes next, and emaciation is the lowest. The appearance should match the feelings; the mournful countenance should match the mourning garments." He then asked about mourning for brothers, and the Master said: "For mourning for brothers, the rules are recorded in the writings." The noble man does not take away others' mourning, nor may his own mourning be taken away. Confucius said: "Shaolian and Dalian were good at observing mourning. For three days they were not remiss, for three months they did not relax, for one year they were sorrowful, and for three years they were grieved. They were sons of the eastern barbarians."

敕天下民庶官吏军兵等：
今上膺天明命，体乾坤之仁，念百姓栉风沐雨之苦。自明日起，赐休假三日。特令各府衙布告中外。与民同享鱼水之欢，共乐太平之化。
庆日兹临，开封府条具三事：
一者，商贾东家，宜体下情，不以阙事克扣。
二者，江湖游侠，宜存礼义，不可踹门催业。
三者，闾里诸坊，宜舞笙歌，不蹈刑宪之律。
故兹诏示，想宜知悉。
en:
Decree to All Commoners, Officials, and Soldiers: 
By the grace of heaven and the benevolence of the cosmos, mindful of the hardships endured by the people, a three-day holiday is hereby granted starting tomorrow. All prefectures and offices are ordered to announce this far and wide. Let all share in the joy of harmony and celebrate this era of peace. 
In observance of this festive occasion, Kaifeng Prefecture decrees the following: 
First, merchants and employers must show compassion and refrain from withholding wages. 
Second, wandering heroes of the martial world must uphold courtesy and refrain from disruptive actions. 
Third, neighborhoods and districts may revel in song and dance, but must not violate the laws. 
Let this decree be known to all.

zh:
世人不知，未央城主东阙公子，实际从未被未央城传授过为商之道。就连温无缺这个字辈上的名字，也并非上任城主温韬所赐，而是她自己取的。
她不是城主温韬的嫡亲女儿，而是温韬妹妹温凝与一孤云弟子的私生女，温韬视此为奇耻大辱，于是草草将温凝许了一个温家忠仆。忠仆得了温家大小姐，便在未央城起了势，得志之后，便是忘恩，对于这别人的孩子，自是打骂不止。
继父凶恶，母亲孱弱，那时她最好的出路，似乎也不过是像其他温家女儿一样，在联姻时赌一个好人家。

可她这孩子从小就有股心气，越是被人看轻，她就越是要争一口气。
于是她不顾母亲劝告，束了头发，扮作男子，便往未央城深处去。摸爬滚打，做小伏低，一步步走到温韬的身边，耳濡目染一出出弱肉强食，她也逐渐懂得，想要站到高处去，就得狠下心来吃人，吃得最多，吃得最快的那个，就会成为这未央城的主人。

她以这颠扑不破的真理，得到了联姻世家的整个家财，还带回了夫君的首级，未央城为之震动，从此，那默默无闻的私生女，成了与温无痕等众公子并提的无缺公子。
别人狠，她就比别人更狠。未央城传言无缺公子最是无常，今日与你谈笑应酬，明日便要取你人头家财，有人甚至觉得温无缺实非一人，所谓黑白财神之说，也是起于那时。敛聚财富的那几年，直接或者间接死在她手里的人不计其数，她从不感到恐惧，只要她常胜，就没有人能将她赶下牌桌。就这样，她闯出温韬为众公子设下的残酷死局，成为新一任的未央城主。

可她忘了，如果她夺走了所有的筹码，那么牌桌就没了存在的必要，而一无所有的温无痕就是那个出手掀翻牌桌的人。
那一日未央城血流成河，温无缺并非无所准备，可终究棋差一着——
质在她手中的温无痕亲眷十几口，全都成了冰冷的尸体，而温无痕手中，却掌着自己的母亲。
“终究是外面的野种，没有未央城的血性。”温无痕大笑着，“没有断腕之勇，岂能做未央城主？”

她无法效法温无痕的狠厉，看着母亲那斑驳的华发，她忽然想到离家那日，她对自己许下的心愿。
“我要走到最高处，让娘再也不受人欺侮。”
她垂下手，买命钱叮当滚落在地，她闭上眼睛，等温无痕了结她的性命，却只听到世界上最可怕的声音——
那是布料与皮肉撕开的声音。是母亲忽的生了蛮力生生撞进了刀尖里。

为何这世上总是事与愿违呢。
en:
The world did not know that the Ember of East, the Lord of Weiyang City, had never been taught the ways of commerce by the city. Even her name, Wuque, meaning "flawless", was not bestowed by the former lord, Wen Tao, but chosen by herself.
She was not Wen Tao's legitimate daughter, but the illegitimate child of his sister, Wen Ning, and a Lone Cloud disciple. Wen Tao regarded this as a grave disgrace, hastily marrying Wen Ning to a loyal servant of the Wen family. The servant, having gained a Wen daughter, rose to power in Weiyang City, but with success came betrayal. He abused the child who was not his own, beating her without mercy.
With a cruel stepfather and frail mother, her fate seemed sealed: gamble on a good marriage like all Wen daughters.

But this child had defiance in her bones. The more they scorned her, the higher she'd climb.
Defying her mother's warnings, she bound her hair, disguised herself as a man, and plunged into the depths of Weiyang City. Through humiliation and scheming, she clawed her way to Wen Tao's side. Witnessing the law of the jungle, she learned that to stand above others, one must be willing to devour ravenously and ruthlessly. The fastest, most relentless eater would rule.

She lived by this creed, seizing the entire fortune of her marital family and returning with her husband's head. Weiyang City trembled. The forgotten bastard became Master Wuque, mentioned in the same breath as Wen Wuhen and other heirs.
If others were ruthless, she was colder. Rumors spread that Master Wuque was capricious: laughing with you today, claiming your head and wealth tomorrow. Some even whispered she was not one person but two, and the legend of the Black and White Gods of Wealth began then. In her years of amassing fortune, countless died directly or indirectly by her hand. She feared nothing, so long as she won. No one could oust her from the game. Thus, she survived Wen Tao's deadly trials for the heirs and became the new Lord of Weiyang City.

But she forgot that if one takes all the chips, the table itself loses purpose. And Wen Wuhen, now penniless, was the one to flip it over.
The day Weiyang City ran red with blood, Wen Wuque was prepared, but not enough.
Over a dozen of Wen Wuhen's relatives in her custody lay dead, while he held her mother hostage.
"You're still a bastard from outside," Wen Wuhen laughed. "No Weiyang blood. Without the courage to sever your own arm, how can you rule?"

She could not match his brutality. Gazing at her mother's silver hair, she recalled the vow she'd made on the day she left home.
"I will climb to the top so no one ever bullies you again."
Her hands fell. The gold coins meant to buy her life clattered to the floor. She closed her eyes, awaiting death, only to hear the most terrifying sound:

zh:
这场仗，我们一定会输。我们所有人，都会死在今天。
烈言看到远处马蹄扬起的沙尘，听到地面隆隆的震动时，如此想到。

烈言读的书不多，他曾只是个清河的浪荡儿，后来，在那个王将军的影响下，他才第一次翻开兵法书。
书上说，用兵之法，十则围之，五则攻之，倍则战之。
却没有说，若是敌方十倍、五倍于自己，该如何胜。
这筹谋已久的最后一战，未免来得太过出乎意料。
“将军！”
“将军！”
“将军！”
将士们都看向他，眼里是同样的茫然和动摇。

“诸位，这门一开，我们便都只有死路。”烈言对着将士们说。
“可若门不开，清河的老少，便只有一条死路。”
眼下，只有最后一条路可走。唯有将敌军尽数引入地下长城，点燃炸药，将敌人和我军，一起埋葬在这燕北盟地下。但这条路也凶险万分，成功的可能微乎其微。
此为利害，悉数告知，所以将士们，你们选什么？
“将军！我愿追随将军，开门，应战！”
“山河寸血，誓死不易！开门，应战！”
“战！”“战！”“战！”
呐喊的声音一浪高过一浪，竟让从未落过泪的烈言生平第一次眼眶湿润。他握紧长枪，将每一张呐喊的脸记在心里，这是最后一眼。

他抹了把脸，转身，将枪尖指向敌军的方向。
“开门——！迎敌！”
他烈言，就活到这。
en:
This battle... will surely be a losing one. All of us will die today.

That is Lie Yan's thought as he watches dust clouds rise from distant hoofbeats and feels the rumbling earth beneath.



Lie Yan is no scholar. Once just a wanderer from Qinghe, it is not until General Wang comes into his life that he first opens a book on the art of war.

The book teaches, "If you outnumber the enemy tenfold, surround them. If fivefold, attack. If double, fight."

But nowhere does it explain how to triumph when the enemy outnumbers you ten to one. Or five.

This long-planned final stand comes more unexpectedly than anyone imagines.

"General!"

"General!"

"General!"

His men look at him, their eyes reflecting the same confusion and wavering resolve.



"Brothers, if we open the gate, we march to our deaths," Lie Yan addresses every one of them.

"But if we don't, the people of Qinghe, every man, woman, and child, will die in our place."

There is only one path left. Lure the enemy into the underground trenches, ignite the explosives, and bury every man-at-arms on both sides beneath the soil in the Northern Vow. A desperate plan with the slimmest chance of success.

"I've told you everything. Now choose. What will you fight for?"

"General! I'll follow you! Open the gate and face them!"

"Our land is worth every drop of blood! Open the gate and fight to the death!"

"To the death!" "To the death!"

The rallying cries grow louder with each wave, bringing tears to the eyes of a man who has never wept before. Gripping his long spear, he memorizes every shouting face. This will be the last time he sees them.



Wiping his face, Lie Yan turns and points his spear toward the enemy.

"Open the gate, and fight to your last breath!"

And that is the last moment of Lie Yan's life.

大葱在文津馆长大。
弟子晨读，它蹲窗棂上听。先生讲经，它趴书案边打盹，半眯着眼，把那些经世道理一句句收进小耳朵里。
日子久了，打翻的墨水也多了，它便觉得自己通文墨，是只文明猫子了。
文明猫子要行文明事。大葱周游青州，四处瞧瞧猫们都在干嘛，顺便搭把手。一来二去，大葱交游遍天下，走到哪儿都有猫跟它打招呼。
如此，青州的猫们遇着难事，都来找它。
哪家小猫被野狗欺负了，大葱便领着它绕三条巷子，专挑有巡逻差役的路走。哪家母猫嫌窝不够软，大葱便教它去风筝铺后院的废料堆里翻。
问题解决了，猫们满意了。
猫们觉得，大葱果真是只顶顶聪明的文明猫！
en:
Leek the cat grew up in the Inkbound Order.
During the disciples' morning recitations, it'd perch on the windowsill and listen. When the master lectured on the classics, it would doze beside the writing desks with its eyes half-shut, letting all that lofty, world-shaping wisdom filter right into its little furry ears.
After soaking in all those lectures and knocking over more than its fair share of inkwells, Leek came to a conclusion: it was a scholar. A feline of letters. A thoroughly civilized cat.
And a civilized cat, naturally, had civic duties. Leek began patrolling the streets of Qingzhou, checking in on the neighborhood strays and lending a paw wherever it could. Before long, it was the most well-connected feline in the city. No matter which alley it strolled down, another cat was always there to nod hello.
Because of this, whenever the cats of Qingzhou ran into a problem, they brought it straight to Leek.
If a nasty stray dog was picking on a kitten, Leek would lead the little guy on a three-alley detour, expertly timing their walk to pass right by the patrolling city guards. If an expecting mother complained the nest wasn't cozy enough, it'd show the cat how to raid the scrap bins behind the kite-maker's shop for soft silk and paper shavings.
Problems were solved, and the feline public was thrilled.
The consensus was clear: Leek was, without a doubt, the cleverest, most civilized cat in town.

After the defense at the pass, Lie Yan heard that the Northern Vow was retreating to Qinghe and rushed to provide support.

for he hoped it would protect Lie Yan and ensure his safe return.
Lie Yan accepted his elder brother's armor and headed to his battlefield.

He had, too, prepared a gift for his brother—a guqin crafted by his own hands.
But due to unfortunate circumstances, it remained at the Qinghe base and was never delivered.
If he returned triumphant, he would surely present this guqin to his brother himself.

Sadly, it was never delivered and now waits in the wilderness for someone destined to find it.

【杂记上第二十】

诸侯行而死于馆，则其复如于其国。如于道，则升其乘车之左毂，以其绥复。其輤有裧，缁布裳帷素锦以为屋而行。至于庙门，不毁墙遂入适所殡，唯輤为说于庙门外。大夫、士死于道，则升其乘车之左毂，以其绥复。如于馆死，则其复如于家。大夫以布为輤而行，至于家而说輤，载以輲车，入自门至于阼阶下而说车，举自阼阶，升适所殡。士輤，苇席以为屋，蒲席以为裳帷。
凡讣于其君，曰：“君之臣某死”；父母、妻、长子，曰：“君之臣某之某死”。君讣于他国之君，曰：“寡君不禄，敢告于执事。”；夫人，曰：“寡小君不禄。”；大子之丧，曰：“寡君之适子某死。”大夫讣于同国：适者，曰：“某不禄”；讣于士，亦曰：“某不禄”；讣于他国之君，曰：“君之外臣寡大夫某死”，讣于适者，曰：“吾子之外私寡大夫某不禄，使某实。”讣于士，亦曰：“吾子之外私寡大夫某不禄，使某实。”士讣于同国大夫，曰：“某死”，讣于士，亦曰：“某死”；讣于他国之君，曰：“君之外臣某死”，讣于大夫，曰：“吾子之外私某死”，讣于士，亦曰：“吾子之外私某死”。大夫次于公馆以终丧，士练而归。士次于公馆，大夫居庐，士居垩室。大夫为其父母兄弟之未为大夫者之丧，服如士服。士为其父母兄弟之为大夫者之丧，服如士服。大夫之适子，服大夫之服。大夫之庶子为大夫，则为其父母服大夫服；其位，与未为大夫者齿。士之子为大夫，则其父母弗能主也，使其子主之。无子，则为之置后。
大夫卜宅与葬日，有司麻衣、布衰、布带，因丧屦，缁布冠不蕤。占者皮弁。如筮，则史练冠长衣以筮。占者朝服。大夫之丧，既荐马。荐马者，哭踊，出乃包奠而读书。大夫之丧，大宗人相，小宗人命龟，卜人作龟。复，诸侯以褒衣冕服，爵弁服，夫人税衣揄狄，狄税素沙。内子以鞠衣，褒衣，素沙。下大夫以襢衣，其余如士。复西上。大夫不揄绞，属于池下。大夫附于士，士不附于大夫，附于大夫之昆弟。无昆弟，则从其昭穆。虽王父母在，亦然。妇附于其夫之所附之妃，无妃。则亦从其昭穆之妃。妾附于妾祖姑，无妾祖姑则亦从其昭穆之妾。男子附于王父则配；女子附于王母，则不配。公子附于公子。君薨，大子号称子，待犹君也。
……
en:
【Miscellaneous Records I (No. 20)】

When a feudal lord dies while traveling and staying at a guesthouse, the calling back of his soul is performed as it would be in his own state. If he dies on the road, they ascend the left hub of his carriage and call back his soul with his reins. His hearse has a canopy with a hem, a black cloth curtain, and a plain silk covering forming a tent-like structure for the journey. When they reach the temple gate, they do not remove the curtain but enter directly to the place of encoffining; only the canopy is removed outside the temple gate. When a great officer or officer dies on the road, they ascend the left hub of his carriage and call back his soul with his reins. If he dies in a guesthouse, the calling back is performed as it would be at home. A great officer uses a cloth canopy for the hearse on the journey; upon arriving home, the canopy is removed, and the coffin is loaded onto a hearse cart, entering through the gate to below the eastern steps, where the cart is unloaded, and the coffin is lifted up the eastern steps to the place of encoffining. For an officer, the hearse uses a reed mat as the tent and a cattail mat as the curtain.
In all announcements of death to one's ruler, it is said: "A minister of your lordship, so-and-so, has died." For a father, mother, wife, or eldest son, it is said: "So-and-so, a minister of your lordship, his [relation] so-and-so has died." When a ruler announces a death to the ruler of another state, it is said: "Our unworthy ruler has not received his full span; I presume to announce this to your officers." For the wife of a ruler, it is said: "Our unworthy little ruler's wife has not received her full span." For the death of the heir apparent, it is said: "The rightful son of our unworthy ruler, so-and-so, has died." When a great officer announces a death to peers in the same state: to one of equal rank, he says: "So-and-so has not received his full span"; to an officer, he also says: "So-and-so has not received his full span." When announcing to the ruler of another state, he says: "So-and-so, the unworthy great officer, a foreign minister of your lordship, has died." When announcing to one of equal rank, he says: "So-and-so, the unworthy great officer, a private acquaintance of yours outside [this state], has not received his full span; I have sent so-and-so to report it." When announcing to an officer, he also says: "So-and-so, the unworthy great officer, a private acquaintance of yours outside [this state], has not received his full span; I have sent so-and-so to report it." When an officer announces a death to a great officer of the same state, he says: "So-and-so has died"; to an officer, he also says: "So-and-so has died." When announcing to the ruler of another state, he says: "So-and-so, a foreign minister of your lordship, has died." When announcing to a great officer, he says: "So-and-so, a private acquaintance of yours outside [this state], has died." When announcing to an officer, he also says: "So-and-so, a private acquaintance of yours outside [this state], has died." A great officer lodges at the ruler's palace to complete the mourning period; an officer returns home after the one-year mourning. When an officer lodges at the ruler's palace, a great officer dwells in a mourning hut, while an officer dwells in a plastered chamber. When a great officer mourns for his father, mother, or brothers who did not hold the rank of great officer, he wears the mourning clothes of an officer. When an officer mourns for his father, mother, or brothers who held the rank of great officer, he wears the mourning clothes of an officer. The rightful son of a great officer wears the mourning clothes of a great officer. If a lesser son of a great officer becomes a great officer himself, he wears the mourning clothes of a great officer for his parents; his position in the mourning rites is ranked with those who have not become great officers. If the son of an officer becomes a great officer, his parents cannot preside over his funeral; they have his son preside over it. If he has no son, then an heir is appointed for him.
When a great officer divines for the burial site and burial date, the attendants wear hempen garments, a hempen mourning sash, and a hempen belt, along with mourning shoes and a black cloth cap without tassels. The diviner wears a skin cap. If they use the yarrow-stalk divination, the scribe wears a plain cap and long robe for the divination. The diviner wears court robes. At the funeral of a great officer, after the horses are presented—when the horses are presented, the mourners wail and leap—then they go out, wrap the offerings, and read the eulogy. At the funeral of a great officer, the chief clansman assists, the lesser clansman charges the tortoise, and the diviner cracks the tortoise. For the calling back of the soul: for a feudal lord, they use the ceremonial robes, the coronation robe, and the cap of the knight; for the wife, the embroidered robe and the plain silk robe; for the inner wife of a great officer, the chrysanthemum robe, the ceremonial robe, and plain silk; for a lower great officer, the unadorned robe; the rest are as for an officer. The calling back is arranged with the west as the place of honor. A great officer does not use the embroidered curtain hanging below the pool [decoration]. A great officer is attached in ancestral sacrifice to an officer; an officer is not attached to a great officer but is attached to the brothers of a great officer. If there are no brothers, then he follows the order of generations (zhao-mu). Even if his grandparents are still alive, this is the same. A wife is attached to the consort of the one to whom her husband is attached; if there is no consort, then she follows the consort of the same generation order. A concubine is attached to the ancestral concubine; if there is no ancestral concubine, then she follows the concubine of the same generation order. When a male is attached to his grandfather, the grandmother is paired with him; when a female is attached to her grandmother, the grandfather is not paired with her. The son of a ruler is attached to the sons of rulers. When the ruler dies, the heir apparent is styled "son," but he is treated as the ruler.
……

晁错峭直，赵禹廉倨。
亮遗巾帼，备失匕箸。
张翰适意，陶潜归去。
魏储南馆，汉相东阁。
楚元置醴，陈蕃下榻。
广利泉涌，王霸冰合。
孔融坐满，郑崇门杂。
张堪折辕，周镇漏船。
郭伋竹马，刘宽蒲鞭。
许史侯盛，韦平相延。
雍伯种玉，黄寻飞钱。
王允千里，黄宪万顷。
虞斐才望，戴渊锋颖。
史鱼黜殡，子囊城郢。
戴封积薪，耿恭拜井。
汲黯开仓，冯驩折券。
齐景驷千，何曾食万。
顾荣锡炙，田文比饭。
稚珪蛙鸣，彦伦鹤怨。
廉颇负荆，须贾擢发。
孔翊绝书，申嘉私谒。
渊明把菊，真长望月。
子房取履，释之结袜。
郭丹约关，祖逖誓江。
贾逵问事，许慎无双。
娄敬和亲，白起坑降。
萧史凤台，宋宗鸡窗。
王阳囊衣，马援薏苡。
刘整交质，五伦十起。
张敞画眉，谢鲲折齿。
盛彦感螬，姜诗跃鲤。
宗资主诺，成瑨坐啸。
伯成辞耕，严陵去钓。
董遇三余，谯周独笑。
将闾仰天，王凌呼庙。
二疏散金，陆贾分橐。
慈明八龙，祢衡一鹗。
不占陨车，子云投阁。
魏舒堂堂，周舍谔谔。
无盐如漆，姑谢若冰。
邾子投火，王思怒蝇。
符朗皂白，易牙淄渑。
周勃织薄，灌婴贩缯。
马良白眉，阮籍青眼。
黥布开关，张良烧栈。
陈遗饭感，陶侃酒限。
楚昭萍实，束晰竹简。
曼倩三冬，陈思七步。
刘宠一钱，廉范五袴。
汜毓字孤，郗鉴吐哺。
苟弟转酷，严母扫墓。
洪乔掷水，陈泰挂壁。
王述忿狷，荀粲惑溺。
宋女愈谨，敬姜犹绩。

en:
【Four】

Nüwa mended the heavens, Changfang shrank the earth.
Jigui was the foremost scholar, Changru a vessel of the state.
Lu Wan had no peer, Jia Xu was out of order.
He Yan was awestruck, Guo Yi was captivated.
Changlin carried the classics, Gaofeng let the wheat float away.
Meng Jia lost his hat, Yu Kai dropped his headscarf.
Long Feng emerged from the plank, Zhang Hua's terrace crumbled.
Dong Feng revived Xie, Bian Que revived Guo.
Kou Xun borrowed one, He Wu departed with thoughts.
Hanzi's solitary indignation, Liang Hong's five sighs.
Cai Yan discerned the qin, Wang Can overturned the chessboard.
Ximen threw the witch, He Qian burned the shrine.
Meng Chang returned the pearl, Liu Kun reversed the fire.
Jiang Gong shared a quilt, Kong Rong yielded the fruit.
Duan and Kang succeeded each other, Liang and Zhi sat apart.
Zhao Lun's owl was strange, Liang Xiao's ox was a calamity.
Huan Dian avoided the horse, Wang Zun scolded the driver.
Chao Cuo was stern and upright, Zhao Yu was incorruptible and aloof.
Liang left women's headgear, Bei dropped his spoon and chopsticks.
Zhang Han followed his heart's desire, Tao Qian returned home.
Wei's heir in the southern lodge, Han's minister in the eastern pavilion.
Chu Yuan set out sweet wine, Chen Fan lowered the couch.
Guangli's spring gushed forth, Wang Ba's ice joined together.
Kong Rong's seat was full, Zheng Chong's gate was crowded.
Zhang Kan broke the shafts, Zhou Zhen's boat leaked.
Guo Ji's bamboo horse, Liu Kuan's cattail whip.
Xu, Shi, and Hou were prosperous, Wei and Ping succeeded each other as ministers.
Yongbo planted jade, Huang Xun's coins flew.
Wang Yun for a thousand li, Huang Xian for ten thousand qing.
Yu Fei's talent and reputation, Dai Yuan's sharpness.
Shi Yu dismissed the funeral, Zi Nang fortified Ying.
Dai Feng piled firewood, Geng Gong bowed to the well.
Ji An opened the granaries, Feng Xuan broke the tallies.
Duke Jing of Qi had a thousand teams of four, He Zeng ate ten thousand.
Gu Rong bestowed roasted meat, Tian Wen compared meals.
Zhigui's frogs croaked, Yanlun's crane lamented.
Lian Po carried thorns, Xu Jia pulled out hair.
Kong Yi ceased correspondence, Shen Jia made private visits.
Yuanming held chrysanthemums, Zhenchang gazed at the moon.
Zifang fetched the shoe, Shizhi tied the sock.
Guo Dan made a pact at the pass, Zu Ti swore at the river.
Jia Kui inquired about affairs, Xu Shen was peerless.
Lou Jing made peace through marriage, Bai Qi buried the surrendered.
Xiao Shi's phoenix terrace, Song Zong's chicken window.
Wang Yang's bagged clothes, Ma Yuan's Job's tears.
Liu Zheng exchanged hostages, Wu Lun rose ten times.
Zhang Chang painted eyebrows, Xie Kun broke a tooth.
Sheng Yan was moved by the grub, Jiang Shi's carp leaped.
Zong Zi presided over promises, Cheng Jin sat and whistled.
Bocheng declined to farm, Yanling left fishing.
Dong Yu's three spare times, Qiao Zhou laughed alone.
Jiang Lü looked up to heaven, Wang Ling called to the temple.
The two Shus scattered gold, Lu Jia divided the sack.
Ciming's eight dragons, Mi Heng's one eagle.
Buzhan fell from the chariot, Ziyun threw himself from the pavilion.
Wei Shu was dignified, Zhou She was outspoken.
Wuyan was like lacquer, Gu Xie was like ice.
The Lord of Zhu threw himself into the fire, Wang Si was angry at a fly.
Fu Lang distinguished black from white, Yi Ya distinguished the Zi and Mian rivers.
Zhou Bo wove mats, Guan Ying sold silk.
Ma Liang had white eyebrows, Ruan Ji had green eyes.
Qing Bu opened the pass, Zhang Liang burned the plank road.
Chen Yi's rice moved hearts, Tao Kan's wine limit.
King Zhao of Chu's duckweed fruit, Shu Xi's bamboo slips.
Manqian's three winters, Chen Si's seven steps.
Liu Chong's one coin, Lian Fan's five pairs of trousers.
Fan Yu cared for orphans, Xi Jian spat out food.
Xun's younger brother became cruel, the stern mother swept the tomb.
Hongqiao threw things into the water, Chen Tai hung on the wall.
Wang Shu was irascible, Xun Can was infatuated.
The Song woman was increasingly careful, Jing Jiang still spun.
Bao Zhao's writings, Chen Lin's proclamations.
Vast are the myriad ages, impossible to fully select.
Prune the profuse, gather the essence, you all strive on.

会同六年，因梦吉兆，阿不里主动请缨，愿随军而战。并在滹沱河畔积薪为坛，为耶律德光的二次柴册礼作准备。鸣铃驱鬼，燔柴告天——契丹将入主中原。
en:
It is said the Khitan forebear came riding east from White Wolf Lake upon a white horse, where he met a heavenly maiden descending the Wolf River in a cart drawn by a blue ox. Where the two waters joined, the eight Khitan tribes were born. Abuli, a princess of the Khitan, was born with white hair and skin like snow, and so was held to be the white horse reborn beneath the gods. From childhood she learned the drum, the whip, and the shaman's art of calling spirits.
In the sixth year of Huitong, after an auspicious dream, Abuli asked to ride with the army. On the banks of the Hutuo River, she raised a wood altar in preparation for Yelu Deguang's second Chai Ce ritual. Bells rang to drive off spirits, and sacred fire rose to heaven—the Khitan were ready to enter the Central Plains.

zh:
《汉书》有云，“骏马名骓。”骓，指毛色苍白相间。乌孙西极中有此纹理者，为金骓。
西汉武帝年间，西域有古国乌孙，不务农耕，以游牧为生，地产良马。《汉书·张骞传》记载：“骞既至乌孙，致赐谕指……乌孙发译道送骞，与乌孙使数十人，马数十匹，报谢，因令窥汉，知其广大。”张骞出使西域，将乌孙骏马带回中原，汉武帝见乌孙马神骏非凡，欣喜万分，名曰“西极”。
乌孙西极体格魁伟，四肢强健，头颅小巧，耳短眸清，外形俊秀。性温顺，耐粗放，春夏时节食草增膘，秋冬时节亦能刨雪觅食，力速兼备，挽乘皆宜，为西域特有的良马马种。
en:
The Book of Han states: "A fine steed is called a zhui", referring to horses with intermingled white and gray hair. Among the Wusun Western Supreme horses, those with such markings were known as Jinzhui - Gold-Gray Charger. 

During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Western Han, the ancient Wusun kingdom in the Western Regions practiced nomadic herding and bred excellent horses. The Book of Han, in the biography of Zhang Qian, records: "Upon reaching Wusun, Zhang Qian conveyed imperial gifts and instructions... Wusun dispatched envoys and dozens of horses with him in return, seeking to better understand the grandeur of the Han." When Zhang Qian returned from his mission, he brought back Wusun steeds. Emperor Wu, struck by their majesty, named them "Western Rarity." 

Wusun Western Rarityhorses are large and muscular, with sturdy limbs, small heads, short ears, and clear eyes, elegant in appearance. Gentle in temperament and hardy in the wild, they fatten on grass in spring and summer, and can dig through snow to feed in autumn and winter. Strong and fast, they are suited for both riding and pulling. They are a prized horse breed unique to the Western Regions.

如果早知道，自己逗笑女子的唯一方法就是手抖，张阿满宁愿她没有治好自己。
至少这样她还会笑一笑。
她一日赛一日地眉头紧锁，好似再没有什么能让她快活。
张阿满好好地把花递给她，把糖饼放桌上，也只能得到她一声叹气。
张阿满急了，整日整夜地睡不着觉，四处打听女子喜欢什么。他托了过路的游侠，直接拦住女子问。
女子叹了口气，游侠不依不饶。
“那便给我带九千九百九十九个月华吧。”
女子说了笑，游侠不当真。
但张阿满当真了。他日日夜夜守着月华，捞着月华，还拉过路人和他一起捞。
是报恩还是爱慕，张阿满早就分不清了。
横竖手不抖了。只要手还好着，他就会一直捞下去。
直到看到她的笑为止。
en:
If he had known that his trembling hands were the only thing that ever made her laugh, Zhang A'man would have chosen never to be cured. At least then, he might still earn a soft giggle from her.
Her brow furrowed more with each passing day, as though nothing in the world could bring her joy anymore.
He offered flowers with steady hands. He set the sugar cakes gently on the table. All he received in return was a quiet sigh.
Desperate, sleepless night after sleepless night, he asked everyone he could what she truly liked. In the end, he requested the help of a wanderer to ask her directly.
She sighed again, but the wanderer pressed her for an answer.
"Well then..." she said lightly, half in jest, "bring me 9,999 pieces of moonlight."
She said it with a laugh, and the wanderer didn't take her seriously either.
But Zhang A'man did. Day after day, night after night, he stood by the water, scooping at the moon's reflection. He even pulled strangers into the effort, asking them to help him gather the scattered light.
Whether it was gratitude or love, he no longer knew.
His hands no longer tremble. And as long as they remained steady, he would keep reaching into the water.
Until the day he could see her smile again.

zh:
《行车安全规范二十条》

第一条：登车之前，先检车轮。轴有裂、辐有松，不得发车。
第二条：系带要紧，坐姿要正。车未停稳，不得起身。
第三条：车速由心，不可逞强。见弯减速，见人鸣号。
第四条：两车交会，左让右行。不得并驾，不得争道。
第五条：夜行须挂灯火。无灯不得出车，有灯不得遮掩。
第六条：雨天路滑，减速缓行。积水之处，绕道为安。
第七条：车上载人，不得过三。载物不得高过头顶、宽过车身。
第八条：驾车之人，不得饮酒。饮酒者，禁车三日。
第九条：行车途中，不得嬉闹。不得回头、不得松缰、不得双手离辕。
第十条：前方有变，先鸣号后转向。鸣号三声，方可行变。
第十一条：跟车须留余地。前车停，后车不得贴其尾。
第十二条：车入棚后，先刹后锁。车轮归位，缰绳挂好。
第十三条：赛中求胜，不可使诈。不得撞车、不得绊马、不得投掷暗器。
第十四条：车有异响，立即停检。不查明缘由，不得复行。
第十五条：练习时段，不得占道。赛场与练道，各分其途。
第十六条：孩童不得驾车。学车者，须有师陪同。
第十七条：车坏于途，须立警示牌。他人见此牌，应绕行相助。
第十八条：比赛之时，服从裁判。判罚既出，不得争辩。
第十九条：遇突发险情，弃车保人。车可再修，人不可再造。
第二十条：以上十九条之外，还有一条——听荆夫子的话。不得嘴上说着知道知道，赛时一条不遵！！！！
凡违反者，轻则罚抄，重则禁车。禁车三次者，取消本年度行车会参赛资格。
en:
Twenty Rules for Safe Driving

Rule 1: Inspect the wheels before boarding. Do not depart if an axle is cracked or a spoke is loose.
Rule 2: Fasten all straps and sit properly. Do not stand until the vehicle has fully stopped.
Rule 3: Control your speed and do not show off. Slow down at bends and sound the horn near pedestrians.
Rule 4: When two vehicles meet, the one on the left must yield. Do not ride abreast or fight for the road.
Rule 5: Carry a lamp when driving at night. Do not depart without one or obstruct its light.
Rule 6: Roads are slippery in the rain. Slow down and avoid flooded areas.
Rule 7: Carry no more than three passengers. Cargo must not rise above your head or extend beyond the vehicle.
Rule 8: Drivers must not drink. Anyone who drinks is banned from driving for three days.
Rule 9: No horseplay while driving. Do not look back, loosen the reins, or take both hands off them.
Rule 10: Before turning or changing course, sound the horn three times.
Rule 11: Keep a safe distance. Never follow too closely behind a stopped vehicle.
Rule 12: Upon entering the shed, brake before locking the vehicle. Align the wheels and hang up the reins.
Rule 13: Compete fairly. Do not ram vehicles, trip horses, or throw concealed weapons.
Rule 14: Stop immediately if the vehicle makes an unusual noise. Do not continue until the cause is found.
Rule 15: Do not obstruct the road during practice. Racing and practice must use separate tracks.
Rule 16: Children may not drive. Learners must be accompanied by an instructor.
Rule 17: If your vehicle breaks down, place a warning sign. Others should steer clear and offer assistance.
Rule 18: Obey the referee during races. Once a ruling is made, do not argue.
Rule 19: In an emergency, abandon the vehicle and save yourself. A vehicle can be repaired; a life cannot be replaced.
Rule 20: One final rule beyond the nineteen above: listen to Master Jing! Don't claim you understand, only to ignore every rule during the race!!!!
Violators will copy the rules as a minor penalty or receive a driving ban for serious offenses. Three driving bans will result in disqualification from this year's competition.

zh: 唐教坊曲名，后用作词调名，《通典》及《乐府杂论》称此曲为隋炀帝将幸江都时，乐工王令言之子所奏，令言闻之流涕言：“宫，君也。宫声往而不返，大驾不复回矣。”据《道理要诀》，唐时《安公子》在太簇角，今已不传。其见于世者，中吕调有近，般涉调有令，然尾声皆无所归宿。
en: A musical piece from the Musicians Institution of the Tang Dynasty, later adopted as a tune pattern for lyrics. According to the Tongdian and Miscellaneous Discussions on Music Bureau, this melody was first played by the son of court musician Wang Lingyan when Emperor Yang of Sui was about to depart for Jiangdu. Upon hearing it, Wang Lingyan wept and said, "Do is the note of the ruler. If the Do departs and does not return, then the imperial carriage shall not return either." According to the Essentials of Way and Reason, during the Tang Dynasty, the piece should be a Tai Tune of Do Temple. While the original composition is now lost, surviving versions include Zhonglü Mode with Jin (an extended form) and Banshe Mode with Ling (a shorter form). However, these transmitted versions all suffer from fragmentary codas.

I

I watch the empty skies for words unsaid.
My youth before a shattered mirror wanes,
And every day of yearning adds new pains.
Cursed is this long life, let it be brief instead.

论剑玩法中有特殊的战斗规则。

论剑中释放卸势会消耗耐力，而处决命中时会回复耐力。

玩家的技能大多都可以以卸势应对，破防奇术不仅不会被卸势，在命中处于防御或在释放卸势技能的目标时，反而有更好的效果，但其可以被任意技能打断。

玩家的各类技能（包括奇术和蓄力技）能够打断轻重击，而反过来则不行。

活用解控技能可以有效扭转劣势。

战胜你的对手可获取论剑积分，积分高的大侠将进入排行榜。

论剑玩法中，玩家造成的治疗效果降低90%。对目标的气血护盾，造成的伤害提升100%。

论剑玩法中闪避的不可选中时长增幅百分比上限为20%

移动端与PC端玩家分开进行匹配，若匹配成功后出现跨平台顶号等异常行为，则该玩家后续匹配将被归入PC端队列。

在限定时间内，率先击败对方的一方获胜，若倒计时结束未分胜负，按以下优先级依次判定：
1.存活玩家数量更多的一方获胜；
2.若存活玩家数量相同，则总伤害量更高一方获胜；
3.若总伤害量相同，则总治疗量更高一方获胜。
en:
Special combat rules apply in the 1v1 Arena mode.

Using Deflect consumes Endurance, while finishing Execute restores Endurance.

Most player skills can be deflected. Defense-breaking Mystic Skills not only ignore deflect but also deal enhanced effects when hitting targets who are defending or deflecting. However, these Mystic Skills can be interrupted by any skill.

Player skills, including Mystic Skills and Charged Skill, can interrupt Light and Heavy Attacks, but not vice versa.

Effective use of Control-breaking Skills can turn the tide.
Defeating your rival grants 1v1 Arena Points. Heroes with the higher points will enter the Arena Leaderboard.

In 1v1 Arena, player's Healing effects are reduced by 90%. Damage to targets' HP Shields is increased by 100%.

In 1v1 Arena, the maximum increase percentage for the untargetable duration of Dodge is capped at 20%.

Mobile and PC players are matched separately. If abnormal activity is detected on a cross-platform account, that player will be queued on the PC platform in future matchmaking.

The side that defeats the opponent first within the time limit wins. If the timer runs out without a decisive outcome, the winner is determined by the following priorities:
 1. The side with more surviving players wins;
 2. If the number of surviving players is equal, the side with the higher total damage dealt wins;
 3. If the total damage dealt is equal, the side with the higher total healing amount wins.

zh:
平日里总是灯火通明的封龙书院，也曾有过那样漆黑的一夜。
那天风雨大作，刮的檐下灯笼一盏接一盏地暗下去，彼时已近冬季，天黑得早，深山的夜晚本就漆黑，封龙书院再暗了，过路人定只剩下心惊胆颤。弟子们商量后，决定轮流守一盏灯。既为了已几日未归的先生，也为了不知是否存在的过路客。至于这值守的顺序嘛，平日斗嘴惯了的几人，当然也要抽签决定。
竹筒摇晃，哗啦作响，风雨声中，竟似妙音。

一更天，刘思农来了。他添油的手很稳，油线笔直注入盏心，很快就生起了一轮光亮。此刻雨幕如瀑。他看了一会儿，从怀里摸出一个小小的粗布包。这样常年贴在他心尖上的物件，他平时可不轻易拿出来——这是他妻儿的坟头土。可此刻四下风雨大作，他竟用双手牢牢地捧着它。只因他想起苗娃在的时候，那么爱看雨。这一刻，四下无人，权当他们还在吧，一家人一起听雨。
二更天，罗成武来了。雨势相较之前缓了些。从前没入院的时候，这个时辰他也醒着，估计正忙着推杯换盏、丝竹乱耳呢。外面的朋友待他好，说得净是他爱听的话。不像这里，每个人的脾气都大得很，特别是那个秦远，真是话不投机半句多……奇怪，怎会在这时想到他？罗成武添上油，靠在窗边，听着雨声淅淅沥沥，竟听出了几分琴韵。这书院时光，好似也不比从前差。
三更天，风雨最狂。一双骨节分明、带着旧疤的粗手，稳住了被狂风吹得乱晃的灯盏。刘小妹来了，她对自己的这双手很满意。曾是马匪的时候，为了活命，她用这双手抽过多少人的嘴巴子！当然，她也知轻重，坏人不收力，好人，做做样子扬起手就是。进了书院，刻起碑来也是一个干脆利落。三更，传说魑魅魍魉最喜此时出没。可刘小妹在此，何方妖孽敢来？
四更天，雨是小些，可寒气渗骨。秦远来了。他裹着薄被，小心翼翼地添油，仿佛多用一滴都是罪过。灯焰重新饱满起来，黄澄澄的光铺开一小圈。他这才从怀里掏出本边角磨烂的书，就着那光，低头看了起来。冷就冷点，自家道中落之后，多得是比此刻更窘迫的境地。能入这封龙书院，已是他一生行的大运。秦远缩了缩肩膀，往灯光里又凑近一点。
五更天，唐文耀来了。这最深最难守的夜，当然得大师兄来。所以他在抽签时悄悄做了些手脚，也无伤大雅吧。他虽是大师兄，却总觉得自己来晚了。他常常感怀，若是能来得更早些就好了。屋外的雨似乎听见了他的心声，忽然变得柔声细语，像是一种安慰。你来得不晚，以后的日子，还长呢……

东方既白之时，风雨归去。
某人打着哈欠走在山道上，鱼竿还是湿漉漉的。
他抬眼，望向不远处的书院——那里竟还存着一盏暖光，那么小，那么稳。
天地正在醒来。
他却顿感此生见过的所有日出时刻、江湖盛景，都不及眼前的这一点光。
真美。
en:
There was once a night when even Dragonbend Academy, usually lit from end to end, fell completely dark.

That day, wind and rain lashed at the mountains, and the lanterns under the eaves went out one after another. Winter was close, so night came early. The mountain dark was deep to begin with, and if Dragonbend Academy lost its light as well, anyone passing by would have little company but fear.
After talking it over, the disciples decided to keep one lamp burning through the night, taking turns to watch it. It was for their teacher, who had been gone for days and still had not returned. It was also for any passerby who might, or might not, be out there in the storm.
As for the order of the watch, well, for a group that argued as often as they did, drawing lots was the only fair way to settle it.
The bamboo tube shook with a rattling clatter. In the storm, it almost sounded musical.

At first watch, Liu Sinong came.

His hand was steady as he poured in more oil, the thin stream falling clean and true, and soon the lamp was glowing again.
The rain was coming down in sheets. He watched it for a while, then took a small rough cloth bundle from inside his robe. He did not take that bundle out lightly. He had carried it close to his heart for years. Inside was earth from the graves of his wife and child.

And yet tonight, with the wind and rain all around him, he held it firmly in both hands.
He had remembered how much Miao used to love the rain. There was no one else around at this hour, so he let himself pretend they were still there with him, the three of them listening to the rain together.

At second watch, Luo Chengwu came.

The rain had eased a little by then. Before he entered the academy, he would still have been awake at an hour like this, probably somewhere amid raised cups and noisy music.
His friends outside had treated him well enough. They always said the things he liked to hear. It was nothing like this place, where everyone had a temper, especially Qin Yuan. The two of them could barely get through a conversation without annoying each other.
Funny. Why think of him now?

Luo Chengwu topped up the oil and leaned by the window. Listening to the rain pattering down, he somehow began to hear a trace of music in it.
Life at the academy, he thought, was not worse than what he had before.

At third watch, the storm was at its worst.
A pair of rough, scarred hands with prominent knuckles steadied the lamp as the wind shook it hard. Liu Xiaomei had arrived.

She liked those hands of hers quite a bit.
Back when she was with the horse bandits, she had used them to slap who knew how many people just to stay alive. Of course, she knew when to hold back. For the truly rotten ones, she never did. For decent people, it was enough just to raise her hand and make a show of it.
After coming to the academy, those same hands took just as neatly to carving stone steles.

People said the third watch was when demons and monsters liked to come out.
But with Liu Xiaomei there, what demon would dare show its face?

At fourth watch, the rain had grown lighter, but the cold had sunk clear into the bone.

Qin Yuan came wrapped in a thin quilt. He added oil with extreme care, as though wasting even one drop would be a sin.
The flame filled out again, casting a small pool of warm yellow light. Only then did he take out a book with worn, frayed corners and lower his head to read by it.

Cold was nothing. Since his family had fallen on hard times, he had known far worse than this.
To have made it into Dragonbend Academy was already the greatest stroke of luck in his life.
Qin Yuan hunched his shoulders and edged a little closer to the light.

At fifth watch, Tang Wenyao came.

The darkest stretch of the night, the hardest one to keep, naturally ought to fall to the senior brother. So when they drew lots, he had quietly tampered with things a little. Harmless enough, surely.
He was the senior brother, and yet he always felt he had come here too late. Many times he had thought how good it would have been if he had arrived sooner.
Outside, the rain seemed to hear what was in his heart. All at once it softened, turning into something almost like a whisper of comfort.

You are not too late.
There is still a long road ahead.

By the time the east began to whiten, the wind and rain were gone.
Someone came walking along the mountain path with a yawn, his fishing rod still wet.

He looked up toward the academy not far ahead.
There was still one warm light burning there, so small, and so steady.
He felt the world around him waking.

And in that instant, every sunrise he had ever seen, every grand sight he had ever known out in the jianghu, seemed to pale beside that one small light before him.

Beautiful.
Qingsong Nian

她站在两座刚立起的坟茔前，把琴供上，又点了一把火。

如果我回来得早一些，是不是还能见到你们最后一面？

Back when Yun Bieqiu was still a proper young lady, she loathed the Guqin.
All that clinking and clattering sounds are painful for the player's fingers, and irritating for the listener's ears. On top of it all, her teacher would scold her mercilessly, while her parents forbade her from talking back.
It was stifling. Utterly so.
Then chaos swept into Qinchuan. Mountains were trampled flat, blossoms cut down, and Yun Bieqiu's home burned.
She stood before two freshly dug graves, placed her Guqin down as an offering, and lit another fire.
See? What use are books and songs now? In the end, they’re nothing compared to a blade.At least a sword draws blood.
If I had come back sooner... would I have seen you one last time?
That day, the world lost a gentle daughter, but gained a wandering blade.

穿山之甲对这一切充耳不闻，独自蜷在一众重盾利器之中，就像它安静的主人一样。
它不知道什么是天才，什么是奇巧。只知道那日，有只迷糊的穿山甲爬过主人的窗前。然后，它便从一截无趣的木头，长出了自己的形状。
en:
The armor is curled up, with a charmingly naive pangolin in the middle, sleeping soundly.
It is so different from Swallow's other creations that the disciples look at each other in disbelief, unable to believe it is the work of that genius.
When it comes to the strength of armor and the sharpness of digging, the pangolin is supreme! The instructor's words caused a stir. Disciples responded enthusiastically, arguing from the relationship between the pangolin and the art of Mohist defense, to how its adorable shape could dishearten the enemy.
The pangolin, however, is oblivious to all this, curled up alone among a host of heavy shields and sharp weapons, just like its quiet owner.
It knows nothing of genius or ingenuity. It only knows that that day, a sleepy pangolin crawled past its owner's window. And then, from a boring piece of wood, it grew into its own shape.

#Y法相。法相有菩萨低眉亦有金刚怒目，以法相示人，则可超脱尘世之外——纵使这只是一个幻想，但你依然希望，他能卸下肩上众任，成为一名世外高人。哪怕须臾也好。#E
禅师并未回答，而是低声颂了句佛号。霎时间，你仿佛看到他身后狂风呼啸，一尊巨大的佛像显露出来。“纵观三相，不如无相。”耳边传来禅师低沉而洪亮的声音。他背后的巨佛像双手合十，风沙隐去了他的身形。待风沙散去，佛光顶上唯有日光彻地，虹彩依然，仿佛禅师从未出现。你不禁怀疑，方才那无相无定之人是否真的折返清河？还是自己这一程入梦又醒，自己产生了幻觉？
en:
Atop Halo Peak, sunlight fractured through the Buddha's Light Jade into drifting rainbow hues. There stood a Chan master, clad half in monk's robes and half in martial garb, Khakkhara staff in hand, as motionless as one of the myriad Buddha statues.
You had heard this master had long since changed his name and journeyed north, yet here, of all places, you unexpectedly crossed paths. His face beneath the mask was entirely unreadable; from afar, you only heard his voice, resonant as a temple bell, asking, "Young patron, do you wish to see my false form, my Dharma form, or my true form?"...
#YDharma form. The Dharma form may hold the lowered gaze of a bodhisattva or the wrathful glare of a vajra. To reveal this form is to transcend the mortal realm. Even if it is but an illusion, you still hope he might shed his heavy burdens and become a worldly transcendent. If only for a fleeting moment.#E
The master gave no answer, but murmured the Buddha's name under his breath. In that instant, howling winds seemed to surge behind him, and the silhouette of a colossal Buddha manifested. "To behold the three forms is not as profound as the formless," the master's low, sonorous voice echoed right beside your ear. Behind him, the great Buddha pressed its palms together, and wind and sand swallowed his form whole. When the wind and sand settled, only sunlight bathed Halo Peak. The rainbows remained unchanged, as if the Chan master had never been there at all. You could not help but wonder whether that formless, unbound man had truly returned to Qinghe. 少牢馈食之礼。日用丁己。筮旬有一日。筮于庙门之外。主人朝服，西面于门东。史朝服，左执筮，右取上韇，兼与筮执之，东面受命于主人。主人曰：“孝孙某，来日丁亥，用荐岁事于皇祖伯某，以某妃配某氏。尚飨！”史曰：“诺！”西面于门西，抽下韇，左执筮，右兼执韇以击筮，遂述命曰：“假尔大筮有常。孝孙某，来日丁亥，用荐岁事于皇祖伯某，以某妃配某氏。尚飨！”乃释韇立筮。卦者在左坐，卦以木。卒筮，乃书卦于木，示主人，乃退占。吉，则史韇筮，史兼执筮与封以告于主人：“占曰从。”乃官戒，宗人命涤，宰命为酒，乃退。若不吉，则及远日，又筮日如初。
宿。前宿一日，宿戒尸。明日，朝服筮尸，如筮日之礼。命曰：“孝孙某，来日丁亥，用荐岁事于皇祖伯某，以某妃配某氏。以某之某为尸。尚飨！”筮、卦占如初。吉，则乃遂宿尸。祝摈，主人再拜稽首。祝告曰：“孝孙某，来日丁亥，用荐岁事于皇祖伯某，以某妃配某氏。敢宿！”尸拜，许诺，主人又再拜稽首。主人退，尸送，揖，不拜。若不吉，则遂改筮尸。
既宿尸，反，为期于庙门之外。主人门东，南面。宗人朝服北面，曰：“请祭期。”主人曰：“比于子。”宗人曰：“旦明行事。”主人曰：“诺！”乃退。
明日，主人朝服，即位于庙门之外，东方南面。宰、宗人西面，北上。牲北首东上。司马圭刀羊，司士击豕。宗人告备，乃退。雍人摡鼎、匕、俎于雍爨，雍爨在门东南，北上。廪人摡甑甗、匕与敦于廪爨，廪爨在雍爨之北。司宫摡豆、笾、勺、爵、觚、觯、几、洗、篚于东堂下，勺、爵、觚、觯实于篚；卒摡，馔豆、笾与篚于房中，放于西方；设洗于阼阶东南，当东荣。
羹定，雍人陈鼎五，三鼎在羊镬之西，二鼎在豕镬之西。司马升羊右胖。髀不升，肩、臂、臑、□、骼，正脊一、横脊短胁一、正胁一、代胁一，皆二骨以并，肠三、胃三、举肺一、祭肺三，实于一鼎。司士升豕右胖。髀不升，肩、臂、臑、□骼，正脊一、横脊一、短胁一、正胁一、代胁一，皆二骨以并，举肺一、祭肺三，实于一鼎。雍人伦肤九，实于一鼎。司士又升鱼、腊，鱼十有五而鼎，腊一纯而鼎，腊用麋。卒脀，皆设扃幂，乃举，陈鼎于庙门之外，东方，北面，北上。司宫尊两甒于房户之间，同棜，皆有幂，甒有玄酒。司宫设罍水于洗东，有枓，设篚于洗西，南肆。改馔豆、笾于房中，南面，如馈之设，实豆、笾之实。小祝设槃、匜与箪、巾于西阶东。
……
en:
【The Sixteenth Ritual of the Lesser Repast Offering】

The ritual of the lesser repast offering. The day is appointed on a ding or ji day. Divination is performed after an interval of eleven days. The divination is conducted outside the temple gate. The host, in court attire, stands facing west to the east of the gate. The recorder, in court attire, holds the divination stalks in his left hand, takes the upper case with his right, and holding both together with the stalks, faces east to receive the command from the host. The host says: "The filial grandson, so-and-so, on the coming day dinghai, will present the annual sacrifice to the great ancestor, Earl So-and-so, with his consort, Lady So-and-so, as the partner. May it be enjoyed!" The recorder says: "Yes!" Facing west to the west of the gate, he removes the lower case, holds the stalks in his left hand, and with his right hand holding both cases, strikes the stalks, then recites the command: "By this great divination, which is constant. The filial grandson, so-and-so, on the coming day dinghai, will present the annual sacrifice to the great ancestor, Earl So-and-so, with his consort, Lady So-and-so, as the partner. May it be enjoyed!" He then sets aside the cases and stands the stalks upright for divination. The hexagram official sits on the left, recording the hexagram on wood. When the divination is complete, he writes the hexagram on the wood and shows it to the host, then withdraws to interpret it. If auspicious, the recorder replaces the stalks in their cases, and holding both the stalks and the hexagram, announces to the host: "The divination says: 'Follow.'" Then the officers are instructed, the ancestral officer orders purification, and the steward orders the preparation of wine, after which they withdraw. If inauspicious, they wait until a later day and divine again for a day, as before.
The Vigil. The day before the vigil, they prepare and instruct the impersonator. On the next day, in court attire, they divine for the impersonator, following the same ritual as divining for the day. The command is: "The filial grandson, so-and-so, on the coming day dinghai, will present the annual sacrifice to the great ancestor, Earl So-and-so, with his consort, Lady So-and-so, as the partner. Let so-and-so, the son of so-and-so, be the impersonator. May it be enjoyed!" The divination, hexagram, and interpretation proceed as before. If auspicious, they then proceed to invite the impersonator. The invocator acts as usher, and the host makes two bows and kowtows. The invocator announces: "The filial grandson, so-and-so, on the coming day dinghai, will present the annual sacrifice to the great ancestor, Earl So-and-so, with his consort, Lady So-and-so, as the partner. We presume to invite you." The impersonator bows and accepts. The host again makes two bows and kowtows. The host withdraws, and the impersonator sees him off with a bow, but does not kowtow. If inauspicious, they then change and divine again for the impersonator.
After inviting the impersonator, they return and set the time outside the temple gate. The host stands to the east of the gate, facing south. The ancestral officer, in court attire, faces north and says: "Please set the time of the sacrifice." The host says: "Let it be as you decide." The ancestral officer says: "Let the service begin at dawn." The host says: "Yes!" Then they withdraw.
On the next day, the host, in court attire, takes his position outside the temple gate, on the east side, facing south. The steward and the ancestral officer face west, with the ancestral officer at the north. The victims are placed with their heads to the north, the first on the east. The master of the horse pierces the sheep, and the master of the officers strikes the pig. The ancestral officer announces that all is prepared, then they withdraw. The cook cleans the tripods, ladles, and stands at the cook's furnace, which is southeast of the gate, with the first on the north. The granary officer cleans the steamers, cauldrons, ladles, and vessels at the granary furnace, which is north of the cook's furnace. The palace officer cleans the dishes, baskets, ladles, goblets, beakers, cups, stools, basins, and baskets beneath the eastern hall, placing the ladles, goblets, beakers, and cups in the baskets; after cleaning, he arranges the dishes, baskets, and baskets in the chamber, placing them to the west; he sets the washing basin southeast of the eastern steps, aligned with the eastern eaves.
When the broth is ready, the cook sets out five tripods, three tripods west of the sheep cauldron, and two tripods west of the pig cauldron. The master of the horse raises the right half of the sheep. The haunch is not raised; the shoulder, arm, upper leg, lower leg, and shank, one central spine, one transverse spine, one short rib, one central rib, one alternate rib, all with two bones joined, three intestines, three stomachs, one lung for lifting, three lungs for offering, are placed in one tripod. The master of the officers raises the right half of the pig. The haunch is not raised; the shoulder, arm, upper leg, lower leg, and shank, one central spine, one transverse spine, one short rib, one central rib, one alternate rib, all with two bones joined, one lung for lifting, three lungs for offering, are placed in one tripod. The cook provides nine pieces of skin and fat, placed in one tripod. The master of the officers also raises the fish and dried meat, fifteen fish to a tripod, and one whole piece of dried meat to a tripod, the dried meat being of elk. When all is arranged, the tripods are fitted with bars and covers, then lifted and set out outside the temple gate, on the east side, facing north, with the first on the north. The palace officer places two wine jars between the door of the chamber, on a shared stand, both covered, with dark wine in one jar. The palace officer sets the water basin east of the washing basin, with a ladle, and places the basket west of the washing basin, facing south. He rearranges the dishes and baskets in the chamber, facing south, as in the presentation of offerings, filling the dishes and baskets with their contents. The minor invocator sets the basin, ewer, basket, and cloth east of the western steps.

en:
Though Skyward City lies in ruins, the skeletal remains of the colossal Peng still whisper of its former glory. How could a Skyward City of such scale crumble overnight? How have its ruins remained suspended, defying gravity and time alike, all these years?
Along the narrow path to Skyward City, you chance upon a fallen kite. Though faded and frayed, a few characters grace its tail. Could they be the owner's name?
#YYing Ning... A vow of serenity. Whose prayers are tethered to these wings?#E
Did this tattered kite once pierce the clouds and part the mists? Did it once soar alongside the drifting clouds and the noble hawks? Did it beat its wings in a final, frantic struggle as it plunged from the heavens?
A kite's destiny lies with the sky; as long as the winds breathe, it shall have its moment to soar once more.

此书能否达于汝手，实未可知。若有幸得阅，当谨记吾诫：速弃功名之念，速置二亩瘠田。躬耕糊口虽艰，然安平胜万金。
en:
By the time you read this scroll, my breath shall have ceased. 
I once served as a humble groom in the Imperial Stables, content merely to tend the steeds. Yet, simply for reporting an official's embezzlement of fodder funds, I was framed as a rebel. Thinking of our departed parents and how we have clung to life together, I could not bear to drag you to the grave with me. Thus, I sought refuge with the Longwu Army.
But they coerced me into driving a carriage through the dead of night to dump a corpse in the wilds. When I checked the deceased inside... it was none other than...
Lowly as I may be, my heart could never brook such treason. Therefore, I have swallowed bitter brine to end my own life. Alas! To think that a lifetime spent taming wild stallions and mastering the blade should end like this, as an unwitting accomplice to regicide! 
I do not know if this letter will ever reach your hands. If luck grants you this sight, engrave my warning upon your heart: Forswear all dreams of rank and fame. Buy a few acres of barren land instead. A peasant's toil may be bitter, but a life of peace outweighs a mountain of gold.

zh:
【成公第八】

元年春，王正月，公即位。
〇二月辛酉，葬我君宣公。
〇无冰。
〇三月，作丘甲。
何以书？讥。何讥尔？讥始丘使也。
〇夏，臧孙许及晋侯盟于赤棘。
〇秋，王师败绩于贸戎。
孰败之？盖晋败之。或曰贸戎败之。然则曷为不言晋败之？王者无敌，莫敢当也。
〇冬十月。

二年春，齐侯伐我北鄙。
〇夏四月丙戍，卫孙良夫帅师及齐师战于新筑，卫师败绩。
〇六月癸酉，季孙行父、臧孙许、叔孙侨如、公孙婴齐帅师，会晋却克、卫孙良夫、曹公子手，及齐侯战于鞍，齐师败绩。
曹无大夫，公子手何以书？忧内也。
〇秋七月，齐侯使国佐如师。己酉，及国佐盟于袁娄。
君不使乎大夫，此其行使乎大夫何？佚获也。其佚获奈何？师还齐侯，晋却克投戟逡巡，再拜稽首马前。逢丑父者，顷公之车右也，面目与顷公相似，衣服与顷公相似，代顷公当左，使顷公取饮。顷公操饮而至，曰："革取清者。"顷公用是佚而不反。逢丑父曰："吾赖社稷之神灵，吾君已免矣。"却克曰："欺三军者，其法奈何？"曰："法斮。"于是斮逢丑父。己酉，及齐国佐盟于袁娄。曷为不盟于师而盟于袁娄？前此者，晋却克与臧孙许同时而聘于齐。萧同侄子者，齐君之母也，踊于棓而窥客，则客或跛或眇。于是使跛者迓跛者，使眇者迓眇者。二大夫出，相与踦闾而语，移日然后相去。齐人皆曰："患之起，必自此始。"二大夫归，相与率师为鞍之战，齐师大败。齐侯使国佐如师。却克曰："与我纪侯之甗，反鲁、卫之侵地，使耕者东亩，且以萧同侄子为质，则吾舍子矣。"国佐曰："与我纪侯之甗，请诺。反鲁、卫之侵地，请诺。使耕者东亩，是则土齐也。萧同侄子者，齐君之母也，齐君之母，犹晋君之母也，不可。请战。壹战不胜，请再。再战不胜，请三。三战不胜，则齐国尽子之有也，何必以萧同侄子为质？"揖而去之。却克瞬鲁、卫之使，使以其辞而为之请，然后许之，逮于袁娄，而与之盟。
〇八月，壬午，宋公鲍卒。
〇庚寅，卫侯速卒。
〇取汶阳田。
汶阳田者何？鞍之赂也。
〇冬，楚师、郑师侵卫。
〇十有一月，公会楚公子婴齐于蜀。
〇丙申，公及楚人、秦人、宋人、陈人、卫人、郑人、齐人、曹人、邾娄人、薛人、鄫人盟于蜀。
此楚公子婴齐也，其称人何？得壹贬焉尔。

……
en:
【Duke Cheng, Year 8】

In the first year of spring, the king's first month, the duke assumed the throne.
In the second month, on Xinyou, we buried our ruler, Duke Xuan.
There was no ice.
In the third month, the丘甲 system was established.
Why is this recorded? To criticize. What is criticized? The initiation of the丘 levy.
In summer, Zang Sun Xu and the Marquis of Jin formed an alliance at Chiji.
In autumn, the king's army was defeated at Maorong.
Who defeated them? It was Jin who defeated them. Some say Maorong defeated them. Then why not say Jin defeated them? The king is invincible; none dare oppose him.
In winter, the tenth month.

In the second year of spring, the Marquis of Qi attacked our northern border.
In summer, the fourth month, on Bingxu, Sun Liangfu of Wei led troops and fought against Qi's army at Xinzhu, and Wei's army was defeated.
In the sixth month, on Guiyou, Ji Sun Xingfu, Zang Sun Xu, Shu Sun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi led troops, joined with Jin Que Ke, Wei Sun Liangfu, and Cao's Prince Shou, and fought against the Marquis of Qi at An, where Qi's army was defeated.
Cao had no high officials; why is Prince Shou recorded? Because of concern for our state.
In autumn, the seventh month, the Marquis of Qi sent Guo Zuo to the camp. On Jiyou, an alliance was made with Guo Zuo at Yuanlou.
A ruler does not send envoys to high officials; why did he send one here? To escape capture. How did he escape? When the army returned the Marquis of Qi, Jin Que Ke threw down his halberd, hesitated, then bowed twice and kowtowed before the horse. Pang Choufu, the right guard of Duke Qing, resembled the duke in face and clothing. He took the duke's place on the left and sent the duke to fetch water. The duke brought water and said, "Fetch the clear kind." The duke used this to escape and did not return. Pang Choufu said, "By the spirits of the altars, our ruler has been spared." Que Ke said, "What is the penalty for deceiving the three armies?" The reply was, "The penalty is beheading." So Pang Choufu was beheaded. On Jiyou, an alliance was made with Guo Zuo of Qi at Yuanlou. Why not ally at the camp but at Yuanlou? Previously, Jin Que Ke and Zang Sun Xu were both on missions to Qi at the same time. Xiao Tong Nizi, the mother of the ruler of Qi, peeked at the guests from a railing, and saw that one was lame and one was blind. So they sent the lame to greet the lame and the blind to greet the blind. The two officials left and talked together at the gate, spending a long time before parting. The people of Qi all said, "Trouble will surely begin from this." The two officials returned and together led troops for the battle of An, where Qi's army was greatly defeated. The Marquis of Qi sent Guo Zuo to the camp. Que Ke said, "Give me the Yan vessel of the Marquis of Ji, return the invaded lands of Lu and Wei, make the farmers till eastward fields, and give Xiao Tong Nizi as a hostage, then I will release you." Guo Zuo said, "Giving the Yan vessel of the Marquis of Ji—I agree. Returning the invaded lands of Lu and Wei—I agree. Making the farmers till eastward fields—this would make Qi's land yours. Xiao Tong Nizi is the mother of the ruler of Qi; the mother of the ruler of Qi is like the mother of the ruler of Jin. This cannot be done. I request battle. If we lose one battle, I request another. If we lose two, I request a third. If we lose three, then all of Qi will be yours. Why must Xiao Tong Nizi be a hostage?" He bowed and left. Que Ke glanced at the envoys of Lu and Wei, had them plead with his words, and then agreed. They met at Yuanlou and formed an alliance.
In the eighth month, on Renwu, Duke Bao of Song died.
On Gengyin, Marquis Su of Wei died.
The fields of Wenyang were taken.
What were the fields of Wenyang? They were the spoils of the battle of An.
In winter, the armies of Chu and Zheng invaded Wei.
In the eleventh month, the duke met with Chu's Prince Yingqi at Shu.
On Bingshen, the duke formed an alliance with the people of Chu, Qin, Song, Chen, Wei, Zheng, Qi, Cao, Zhulou, Xue, and Zeng at Shu.
This was Chu's Prince Yingqi; why is he called "person"? To give one degree of censure.

【风】

咏风

微雨夜行

【露】

玉阶怨

玉阶生白露，夜久侵罗袜。

月夜忆舍弟

有弟皆分散，无家问死生。

韦应物

【雾】

雾

曹公迷楚泽，汉帝出平城。
涿鹿妖氛静，丹山霁色明。

en:
【Astronomy · II】

【Wind】

Ode to the Wind
Wang Bo
Cool winds arise, solemn and still,
Bringing freshness to my woods and hill.
They chase the mist from the valley's door,
And sweep the fog from the mountain's floor.
Coming and going, they leave no trace,
Yet in their motion, a gentle grace.
As sunset calms the land and stream,
They stir the pines with whispered dream.

Wind
Li Qiao
It strips the leaves in autumn's fall,
And makes the flowers in springtime call.
It whips the river into waves so high,
And bends the bamboo, making it sigh.

【Rain】

Good Rain on a Spring Night
Du Fu
Good rain knows its season right,
It comes with spring, a welcome sight.
It sneaks in on the wind by night,
And moistens all things with delight.
The country paths are dark with cloud,
A lone boat's lamp shines bright and proud.
At dawn, the red and dampened ground,
With flowers heavy, will be found.

West Creek at Chuzhou
Wei Yingwu
Alone, I love the grass by the creek,
A yellow oriole sings, its voice unique.
Spring tides bring rain, swift and deep,
At the wild crossing, a boat lies asleep.

Walking at Night in Light Rain
Bai Juyi
Autumn clouds rise, vague and gray,
A slight chill grows as night holds sway.
I only feel my clothes grow damp,
No sound or drop, a gentle stamp.

【Dew】

Grievance on the Jade Steps
Li Bai
White dew forms on the steps of jade,
So late at night, my silk socks fade.
I lower the crystal screen,
And gaze at the autumn moon, serene.

Thinking of My Brother on a Moonlit Night
Du Fu
The war drum cuts the traveler's way,
A lone goose cries in autumn's sway.
Dew turns white from tonight's air,
The moon at home is brighter there.
My brothers are scattered far and wide,
No home to ask if they've died.
Letters seldom reach their place,
And war still shows no sign of grace.

Ode to the Dewdrop
Wei Yingwu
A single drop on autumn's lotus leaf,
Falls from the dark sky in the night, brief.
Placed on a jade plate, it will roll,
Only then its perfect circle is whole.

【Fog】

Fog
Li Qiao
Lord Cao was lost in Chu's marshland,
The Han emperor left Pingcheng, grand.
At Zhuolu, evil airs grew still,
On Dan Mountain, bright colors spill.
Like smoke, it flies, a bit too dense,
Like rain, it scatters, light and immense.
If it foretells a hero's rise,
Would one think of the dark leopard's guise?

Walking Through the Fog
Wei Yingwu
Autumn city, sea fog thick and deep,
Duty calls at dawn, from sleep I leap.
Vast, it merges with the primal sky,
Blurring the bright sun, passing by.
Just seen, it whitens hair and brow,
Soon clothes are damp, I feel it now.
Paths and riders lost from sight,
Country trees vanish in the white.
A faint breath wrong, a chilling dread,
My skin grows cold, with fear I'm fed.
Returning home, I'll drink a cup,
Hoping this ailment to give up.

zh:
吾近一生栖于不见山中，林壑万籁，渐谙于心。
犹记初入山门，伫#Y入山口#E闻草木萌芽之声，纤微若天籁，至今萦怀，此亦为后日结合乐社之初心。
后虽供职#Y沦波坊#E，昔年同侪谐律之清音、#Y墨守亭#E辩经之铿锵，于记忆中亦未有一日停歇。
然岁徙事迁，人各赴途，散聚难期……
可四时流转，声景相续，又萌一念，何不制一留声机巧。
智与木石同律，人偕机巧共生。
墨门非乐，非绝五音，实以生民为本，艺事次之。
今欲以自然韵律载墨家之思，凭留声机巧复录墨道日常之声景。
或能存当下之美好，更将心中未解之悬问，留予后来之人。

此问为：墨道……何声？

穷尽此生，但求一闻。
然墨道之声，丰沛如川海。
可吾之一生，浅淡若草痕。
转瞬白首，诸响渐寂，惟#Y书斋#E狸奴偶尔轻唤，伴此残年。
今之后学，多争辩开山、封山之径，忆中#Y七色坪#E上众声谐和之景，恐难再逢。
若有来者愿持此匣，续探墨道之声，吾心……甚慰……
en:
For most of my life, I have dwelt within Hidden Mountain. Over time, the voices of woods and ravines, of all things sounding together, have slowly become familiar to my heart.
I still remember my first entry through the mountain gate. Standing at the #YMountain Verge#E, I heard the sound of grasses and trees putting forth new shoots, so faint and delicate that it seemed like music from Heaven itself. To this day it still lingers in my heart. That first stirring in the heart was what later led me to found the Harmony Troupe.
Though I later served at #YDeepwave Works#E, the pure notes of those companions who once sought harmony with me, and the ringing force of the debates at #YConfluence Gazebo#E, have never for a single day fallen silent in memory.
Yet as the years passed and all things changed, each went his own way, and meetings and partings alike became hard to foretell.
Still, as the seasons turn and sound and scene follow one another, a thought has taken root. Why not fashion a device that preserves sound?
If wisdom shares one law with wood and stone, then man and mechanism may dwell in accord as well.
The Mohists do not prize music, yet neither do we reject the five tones. We take the people's livelihood as our root, and the arts as secondary.
Now I wish to set the thought of the Mohist Dao to the rhythms of the natural world, and by means of this sound-preserving device, record once more the everyday soundscape of Mohist Hill.
Perhaps it may preserve the beauty of the present hour, and also leave to those who come after an unanswered question that has long remained in my heart.

That question is this: what sound does the Mohist Dao make?

If I may hear it but once in this lifetime, that will be enough.
And yet the Mohist Voice is abundant as rivers and seas, while my own life is faint and slight as the trace of grass.
In but a moment, my hair has turned white. One by one, all sounds grow still. Only the little cat in my #Ystudy#E gives the occasional soft cry, keeping me company in these fading years.
Among those who study after me, many now dispute the roads of opening the mountain and sealing the mountain. I fear the harmony of many voices once heard upon #YSeven-Hued Plain#E may never again be found.
If someone should come after me, willing to take up this casket and continue the search for the Mohist Voice, then my heart... would be greatly comforted.
Is there something I can help with?

挖井劳苦，不知结果，耗费时日亦无法计数。若想中途退出，可至贺家人处领一份谋生费，自行离开便可。
此后若再有可行之法，需于此记录，随挖井使用之油灯，代代相传，以护后人。
马头村诸人，皆读此诀，以此为誓。
en:
To prevent further collapses, the villagers of Horsehelm Village gathered to discuss and formulated three tips, which were implemented immediately. 
Now recorded in writing, all those involved in well digging must keep them firmly in mind. 
Firstly, personnel above ground must closely monitor surface wind and sand conditions. If strong winds are observed and the air feels piercingly cold, this is a sign of an impending major sandstorm. Immediately send someone down the well to notify everyone. All diggers must ascend to the surface without delay. 
Secondly, personnel below ground shall be divided into two groups. Group One continues digging the well, and Group Two follows closely behind, constructing the passageway. Regardless of the materials or methods used, the passage must be made sturdy to secure time for returning to the surface. 
Thirdly, no matter what important matters arise, internal strife is forbidden. 
Well digging is arduous labor, with uncertain outcomes and countless days expended. Anyone wishing to withdraw partway may go to the He family to receive a subsistence allowance and leave on their own accord. 
If additional viable methods are discovered hereafter, they must be recorded here and passed down along with the oil lamps used for well digging, from generation to generation, to protect future workers. 
All members of Horsehelm Village have read these principles and swear by them.

zh:
“香蒲，你在写什么？”
“故、故事……侠客的故事。”
“侠客，我看看……侠客是这样讲话的吗？你见过侠客吗？”
“没……”
“没见过的，怎么写成故事？”

故事。什么是故事？
小时候赶集，搬着板凳坐在说书人脚边，听得入迷的“王侯将相，宁有种乎”是故事吗？趴在学堂窗底，借着接弟弟的名义，偷听到的那句“十步杀一人，千里不留行”是故事吗？话本铺子那些被斥为难登大雅之堂，却被她偷偷藏在枕下的《虬髯客传》《李寄斩蛇》……这样的武侠话本是故事吗？如果这些是故事，那这些故事里，有我想成为的人吗？它们是怎么被写出来的？我要怎样才能写出这样的故事呢？

香蒲不知道。
香蒲只能写，一直写。
在深宫里，日复一日地扫着永远扫不完的落叶，看着天空一点点变黑，太苦了。听老宫女说，从前乱的时候，谁谁谁昨儿还在笑，今儿就被卷在草席里抬出去了，太怕了。好不容易写出来的话本子，被管事姑姑撕得粉碎，扔在脸上，太疼了。
除了忍受这种苦、这种害怕、这种疼痛，她又能到哪里去呢？回到那个为了几贯钱就把她卖给别人的家吗？还是认命，在这个深宫里待到死呢？
天地这样大，为何她感觉自己无处可去呢？

她只好写。写自己从未见过的江湖，写梦里都不敢想的快意恩仇，写那个永远不会来救她的黑衣大侠……直到她写出了璎璎。
璎璎也是宫女，可璎璎最后翻出了宫墙，成为了大侠。璎璎可以，为什么我不可以？
……就算今天写不出好故事，但只要坚持写，总有一天能写出来的吧。就像璎璎，在话本里一次又一次尝试出宫，总会想到办法的对不对？

“精卫衔微木，将以填沧海。一岁不成，则期十载。此生不成，亦无悔也。”
她会成为“璎璎”的。
en:
"What are you writing, Xiangpu?"
"A... a story. A tale of wanderers."
"Wanderers? Let me see... Do they really speak like this? Have you ever even encountered one?"
"No..."
"If you've never seen one, how can you weave a story about them?"

A story. What constitutes a story?
She remembered when she was a child, she sat on a stool by the storyteller's feet at the market, who spoke of the enthralling cry of "Are kings and nobles born to their high stations?" Was that a story? Crouching by the schoolroom window under the guise of fetching her brother, she overheard the line, "A life taken every ten paces, a thousand miles traveled without a trace." Was that a story? And what about the tales of wandering grandmasters, which were deemed too crude for refined tastes yet were hidden beneath her pillow? If these were stories, was there anyone within them I yearned to become? How were they crafted? And how could I summon such a tale from my own brush?

Xiangpu did not know.
She could only write on and on, without end.
In the depths of the palace, sweeping endless leaves day after day while watching the sky wither into darkness was too bitter. The elder maids whispered of chaotic times, where one might be laughing yesterday only to be carried out today, shrouded in a coarse straw mat. It was too frightening. The storybooks she struggled to write ended up being torn to shreds by the head matron and flung into her face. It was too painful.
Beyond enduring this bitterness, this dread, this pain, where else could she turn? Back to the home that bartered her away for a few strings of coins? Or resign herself to fate, wilting within these high walls until death?
The world is so vast; why, then, did she feel there was no place for her in it?

She had no choice but to write. She wrote of the jianghu she had never seen, of the bold vengeance and gratified debts she dared not even dream of, of the hero in black who would never come to her rescue... until she wrote Yingying into existence.
Yingying was a palace maid as well, yet she eventually leaped over the palace walls and became a great heroine. If Yingying could, why couldn't I? Even if a good story eludes me today, as long as I keep working at it, I'll make it someday, won't I? Just like Yingying, attempting to escape the palace time and again within those pages, there must be a way out, right?

"The Jingwei bird carries twigs to fill the vast sea. If one year fails her, she looks ahead to ten; if this life fails her, she holds no regrets."
She shall become "Yingying."

zh:
（一）
今日卯时，钱一贯迟到一次，本旬共一次，记名！
今日卯时，刘十三迟到一次，本旬共三次，记名！
今日卯时一刻，郭安迟到一次，本旬共一次，记名！
这个刘十三，夜里巡查总不在铺上躺着，竟然偷偷溜出去训练，可见此人心机之深！不过，一旬迟到三次实在是太多了，给他改改，万一到时候头儿一生气把他调过来代替我咋办？
（二）
这个吴不响，又被人告了一状，很了不起吗？整天把自己是哪里人挂在嘴边上。一巴掌！
还有这个丁默，别人跟你多说几句话就找我告状，也给一巴掌！
冯成，大呼小叫，一巴掌！
任捷，钱一贯不搭理他了也来问我怎么办，一巴掌！
老天，快让头儿想起我的好来，把我调回去，我就再也不用给这群人处理纠纷了！（小字注：老天，我是随口一说，别当真啊！）
（三）
有意思吗？戏耍我很好玩吗？夜里不知道哪里传来鬼哭狼嚎的声音，我以为鬼来了呢！勇敢跑过去保护他们，谁知道是时连又被哪个宫人拒绝了，正在哭！
（后面标注一小行字，似是隔段时间后新加的：有完没完了，时连！唉，当时写这段的时候也没想到，时连哭了这么久，哭得比冬天刮的风还吓人，都有不少人找我告状了，真是钱难挣屎难吃，还得管这个。）
（四）
诶，这殿前司的刘横，咋每天都来找石实啊？此事必有蹊跷，盯住他！难不成我武德司有人和殿前司暗通款曲？嗯，待我弄明白了告诉老大，升职有望啊！
（后面标注一小行字，似是隔段时间后新加的：闲的，浪费时间看他俩，呸！）
（五）
听说头儿要把韩远那个木头调过来替我，真是岂有此理！那、那我去哪呢！
这可是万中无一的好差事啊！
话又说回来了，遥想当初，头儿给我一群侍卫的画像，要我记住哪个名字对应哪张脸，我以为我这过目不忘的本事终于有用武之地了，谁知道是干这个啊！唉，算了，珍惜这段日子吧，怎么说也算为武德司做贡献了嘛……
（六）
真是大胆！竟有人在我眼皮子底下买外食！买就买了，还来告状说有贼人偷了他的外食，问我看没看见，笑话！我一天到晚还得盯着这事，把我当什么了！我汤鑫——只负责点卯！
（七）
冬天好冷，就像我的心一样，还是我的椅子舒服，铺上旧衣裳，暖和！
看看之前写的，真有意思，乐！唉，其实和这些人共事也挺有意思，一想到他们被头儿训一顿，我就想笑！
汤鑫我，会一直盯着你们的——
en:
I
Mao hour today:
Qian Yiguan: late once. Total this ten-day period: 1. Recorded.
Liu Shisan: late once. Total this ten-day period: 3. Recorded.
A quarter into Mao hour:
Guo An: late once. Total this ten-day period: 1. Recorded.

That Liu Shisan never stays on his pallet during night watch. Sneaks out to train instead. Calculating, that one.
Still, three late marks in ten days is too much. I should straighten him out a bit. If the chief gets fed up and transfers him here to replace me, what then?

II
Wu Buxiang got reported again. Think you're impressive? And stop yapping about where you're from. Slap.
Ding Mo, someone chats with you for two extra lines and you come running to me to complain. Slap.
Feng Cheng, shouting your head off. Slap.
Ren Jie, Qian Yiguan stops talking to you and you ask me what to do. Slap.

Heavens, please let the chief remember how good I am and transfer me back. I am so done settling disputes for this lot.
(Small note: Heavens, I was just saying it. Don't take it seriously.)

III
Is this funny? Toying with me, is that a good time?
Somewhere in the night I heard wailing, like ghosts. I ran over to protect them.
Turns out Shi Lian got turned down by some palace attendant again. Crying his eyes out.

(A short line added later, as if written much later:
Enough already, Shi Lian. Sigh. When I wrote this, I didn't think he'd keep crying for so long.
Louder than the winter wind, and now people are filing complaints with me about it.
This job pays dirt, and I still have to deal with this.)

IV
Hey. Why does Liu Heng from the Palace Guard come looking for Shi Shi every single day?
Something's off. Keep an eye on him.
Could someone in the Imperial Service be cozying up to the Palace Guard?
If I figure it out and report it to the boss, a promotion might be within reach.

(A short line added later, as if written much later:
What a waste of time, watching those two. Bah.)

V
I heard the chief wants to transfer that wooden block Han Yuan over to take my place. Outrageous. Then where does that leave me?
This is a once-in-a-lifetime posting.

Still, thinking back. The chief once handed me a stack of guard portraits and told me to memorize every name with every face.
I thought my "never forget a face" talent was finally going to shine. Who knew this was the job?
Ah well. Cherish these days. One way or another, I'm doing my part for the Imperial Service.

VI
The nerve. Someone bought outside food right under my nose.
Fine, buy it. But then he came whining that a thief stole it, and asked if I'd seen anything. What a joke.
Am I supposed to watch that too, all day long? What do they take me for?
I, Tang Xin, am only responsible for roll call.

VII
Winter's freezing. Just like my heart.
Still, my chair is nice. Throw an old coat over it warm.

Reading what I wrote before, it's actually pretty funny. Ha.
Honestly, working with these people is kind of fun too. Every time I picture the chief chewing them out, I can't help laughing.
Tang Xin here will be keeping an eye on you all. Always.

zh:
麦芽糖喜欢嗅着锅气晒太阳，也喜欢晒月亮，晒自己圆滚滚的肚皮。它觉得家真好，总有人来来往往，带来食物的香气。
唯独有一个人，只在深夜前来。她带来的饼子总是冰冰凉、咸津津的，那是眼泪的味道。麦芽糖看见她一边掰饼一边哭，明明那么伤心，却还是分了一半给自己。它知道，她在想家，就像自己只想窝在柴火垛旁打盹一样。
饼子吃在嘴里有些发苦，麦芽糖悄悄伸出爪子搭在她膝头，钻出一颗毛茸茸的脑袋，哼哼唧唧地望着她。即便她听不懂，也一定能知晓：这点温热的陪伴，就是麦芽糖给她的甜。
en:
Malt likes to bask in the warmth of the kitchen, nose full of pot steam. It also likes to bask in the moonlight, proudly showing off its round belly.

Home feels wonderful to Malt. People come and go, and every passing footstep brings another hint of food.

There is only one exception: someone who visits just before midnight. The flatbread she brings is always cold, and faintly salty. It tastes like tears.

Malt watches her cry as she breaks the bread apart. She is clearly heartbroken, yet she still gives half to Malt. It knows she is thinking of home, the same way Malt only wants to curl up and doze beside the woodpile.

The bread is a little bitter. Malt quietly rests a paw on her knee, nudges in with its fluffy head, and looks up at her, making small, pleading sounds.

Even if she cannot understand, she is sure to know. This small warmth of companionship is the sweetness Malt can give.

【国风·周南·上】

关雎

关关雎鸠，在河之洲。窈窕淑女，君子好逑。
参差荇菜，左右流之。窈窕淑女，寤寐求之。
求之不得，寤寐思服。悠哉悠哉，辗转反侧。
参差荇菜，左右采之。窈窕淑女，琴瑟友之。
参差荇菜，左右芼之。窈窕淑女，钟鼓乐之。

葛覃

葛之覃兮，施于中谷，维叶萋萋。黄鸟于飞，集于灌木，其鸣喈喈。
葛之覃兮，施于中谷，维叶莫莫。是刈是濩，为𫄨为绤，服之无𭣧。
言告师氏，言告言归。薄污我私，薄澣我衣。害澣害否，归宁父母。

卷耳

采采卷耳，不盈顷筐。嗟我怀人，置彼周行。
陟彼崔嵬，我马虺𬯎。我姑酌彼金罍，维以不永怀。
陟彼高岗，我马玄黄。我姑酌彼兕觥，维以不永伤。
陟彼砠矣，我马瘏矣，我仆𤸵矣，云何吁矣。

樛木

南有樛木，葛藟累之。乐只君子，福履绥之。
南有樛木，葛藟荒之。乐只君子，福履将之。
南有樛木，葛藟萦之。乐只君子，福履成之。

螽斯

螽斯羽，诜诜兮，宜尔子孙，振振兮。
螽斯羽，薨薨兮，宜尔子孙，绳绳兮。
螽斯羽，揖揖兮，宜尔子孙，蛰蛰兮。
en:
[Odes: Zhou South: I]

Guan Ju

Hark! from the islet in the stream the voice
Of the fish-hawks that o'er their nest rejoice!
From them our thoughts to that young lady go,
Modest and virtuous, loth herself to show.
Where could be found, to share our prince's state,
So fair, so virtuous, and so fit a mate?
See how the duckweed's stalks, or short or long,
Sway left and right, as moves the current strong!
So hard it was for him the maid to find!
By day, by night, our prince with constant mind
Sought for her long, but all his search was vain.
Awake, asleep, he ever felt the pain
Of longing thought, as when on restless bed,
Tossing about, one turns one's fevered head.
Here long, there short, afloat the duckweed lies;
But caught at last, we seize the longed-for prize.
The maiden modest, virtuous, coy, is found;
Strike every lute, and joyous welcome sound.
Ours now, the duckweed from the stream we bear,
And cook to use with other viands rare.
He has the maiden, modest, virtuous, bright;
Let bells and drums proclaim our great delight.

Ge Tan

Sweet was the scene. The spreading dolichos
Extended far, down to the valley's depths,
With leaves luxuriant. The orioles
Fluttered around, and on the bushy trees
In throngs collected—whence their pleasant notes
Resounded far in richest melody.
The spreading dolichos extended far,
Covering the valley's sides, down to its depths,
With leaves luxuriant and dense. I cut
It down, then boiled, and from the fibres span
Of cloth, both fine and coarse, large store,
To wear, unwearied of such simple dress.
Now back to my old home, my parents dear
To see, I go. The matron I have told,
Who will announcement make. Meanwhile my clothes,
My private clothes I wash, and rinse my robes.
Which of them need be rinsed and which need not?
My parents dear to visit, back I go.

Juan Er

Though small my basket, all my toil
Filled it with mouse-ears but in part.
I set it on the path, and sighed
For the dear master of my heart.
My steeds, o'er-tasked, their progress stayed,
When midway up that rocky height.
Give me a cup from that gilt vase,
When shall this longing end in sight?
To mount that lofty ridge I drove,
Until my steeds all changed their hue.
A cup from that rhinoceros' horn
May help my longing to subdue.
Striving to reach that flat-topped hill,
My steeds, worn out, relaxed their strain;
My driver also sank oppressed:
I'll never see my lord again!

Jiu Mu

In the South are the trees whose branches are bent,
And droop in such fashion that o'er their extent
All the dolichos' creepers fast cling.
See our princely lady, from whom we have got
Rejoicing that's endless! May her happy lot
And her honours repose ever bring!
In the South are the trees whose branches are bent,
And droop in such fashion that o'er their extent
All the dolichos' creepers are spread.
See our princely lady, from whom we have got
Rejoicing that's endless! Of her happy lot
And her honours the greatness ne'er fade!
In the South are the trees whose branches are bent,
And droop in such fashion that o'er their extent
All the dolichos' creepers entwine.
See our princely lady, from whom we have got
Rejoicing that's endless. May her happy lot
And her honours complete ever shine!

Zhong Si

Ye locusts, winged tribes,
Gather in concord fine;
Well your descendants may
In numerous bright hosts shine!
Ye locusts, winged tribes,
Your wings in flight resound;
Well your descendants may
In endless lines be found!
Ye locusts, winged tribes,
Together cluster strong;
Well your descendants may
In swarms for ever throng!
